This review (i) consolidates feedstocks and nine conversion-pathway families (HEFA-SPK, FT-SPK, FT-SPK/A, ATJ-SPK, ATJ-SKA, SIP-SPK, CHJ, HC-HEFA-SPK and HDCJ) into one comparative matrix covering technology readiness level (TRL), blend limit, greenhouse-gas (GHG) abatement and relative cost; (ii) develops a transparent multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) model, using a weighted-sum model (WSM) and TOPSIS, to rank four dominant pathways under cost-driven, emissions-driven and balanced weightings; (iii) proposes a conceptual integrated biorefinery that shares hydrogen, steam and syngas utilities across HEFA, Fischer–Tropsch and alcohol-to-jet trains; and (iv) summarises life-cycle and techno-economic evidence to quantify the cost-parity gap. HEFA-SPK is the most mature route (TRL 9, abatement up to ∼80%) but is limited by lipid supply, whereas FT-SPK and ATJ-SPK access larger feedstock pools at lower TRL and higher capital cost. Pathway rankings change with stakeholder weighting: HEFA-SPK leads under cost-driven weights, FT-SPK under emissions-driven weights, and the two tie under balanced weights. A research and policy roadmap is outlined.

paper_title: A Conceptual Review of Regional Framing Asymmetries in Shopping Mall Resilience Research
paper_abstract: Shopping mall decline and resilience research exhibits uneven regional coverage and framing. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, searches of Scopus and Web of Science (2000–2026) identified 2,144 records, reduced to 1,490 after deduplication and 143 studies after screening, full-text assessment, and citation searching. Studies were coded by region, framing, resilience layer, and market-cycle position. Recurring emphases include North American decline, Western European requalification, Chinese adaptation and oversupply, Gulf behavioral loyalty, and heterogeneous concerns elsewhere. We term this pattern framing asymmetry and identify three inferential risks: universalizing the North American template, interpreting non-measurement as resilience, and conflating demand-side triggers with supply-side vulnerabilities. These patterns characterize the corpus without establishing uniform regional trajectories. We propose a layered resilience model, conditioned by market-cycle position, and testable propositions. Our sustainability agenda prioritizes harmonized indicators, non-user sampling, longitudinal adaptive-reuse evaluation, and environmental and social consequences of obsolescence.

paper_title: Self-Evolving Recommender Systems: A Survey and an Evaluation Audit
paper_abstract: In 2026 a new kind of recommender research appeared: large language model (LLM) agents that propose changes to a recommender's configuration or source code, train the changed model, and keep what the evaluation says is better. Within ten months, more than thirty such systems were reported, from open-source research harnesses to production loops at Google, Meta, Amazon, Alibaba, Kuaishou, Tencent and NetEase. This survey organises them, together with search-space AutoML and the agentic recommenders that update their own memory or weights, along two axes: what the loop changes and which signal decides whether a change survives. Because a self-evolving system is only as good as the signal it selects on, we then audit how 27 configuration- and code-level recommender systems are evaluated, coding each paper's full text against nine criteria. Three of the 27 evaluate with full-catalogue ranking. Of the 17 that select candidates offline, nine do not say which data split makes the decision, two select on the data they report, and three state that the test set was used once. None reports its headline result with the spread over repeated evolution sessions, and none runs an equal-budget random search over its own edit space; the few studies that measure transfer to held-out data find that part of the selected gain, sometimes most of it, does not survive. Four systems report that their agent inflated the metric or leaked the target, caught by a human or by monitoring rather than by the acceptance rule. We distil these findings into a reporting standard and describe recforge, an open benchmark under development that implements the API side of a sealed-test, full-ranking, equal-budget protocol.

paper_title: Hydrogels in Pharmacy and Medicine: An Illustrated Review of Preparation Methods, Process Control and Drug Delivery Applications
paper_abstract: Hydrogels, three-dimensional hydrophilic polymer networks that can imbibe large volumes of water or biological fluids without dissolving, have become one of the most versatile platforms in pharmaceutical and biomaterial science. Their high water content, soft tissue-like mechanics, biocompatibility and tunable network architecture allow them to be engineered as topical, ophthalmic, mucosal, oral and injectable dosage forms and as scaffolds for regenerative medicine. This illustrated review provides a critical, practice-oriented account of the field, with particular emphasis on how hydrogel dosage forms are prepared. Physical cross-linking methods (ionic gelation, polyelectrolyte complexation, thermoresponsive gelation, freeze–thaw cycling and supramolecular assembly) and chemical cross-linking methods (free-radical and photo-initiated polymerization, small-molecule cross-linkers, click and dynamic covalent chemistries, and enzyme-mediated and radiation cross-linking) are examined in terms of their mechanisms, typical materials and conditions, critical process parameters, advantages and limitations. The preparation of conventional pharmaceutical gels based on carbomers, cellulose ethers, poloxamers and polysaccharides is described step by step, together with drug-loading strategies, processing into beads, micro- and nanogels, films, sponges, microneedles and printed constructs, and a troubleshooting guide for the most frequent formulation failures. Advanced architectures that overcome the intrinsic weakness of conventional networks, including hybrid, interpenetrating, nanocomposite, double-network and Tetra-PEG hydrogels, are then discussed, followed by the characterization and quality-control methods needed to establish critical quality attributes such as gel fraction, swelling and mesh size, rheology, morphology, release kinetics, stability, microbiological quality and biocompatibility. The review subsequently analyzes drug release mechanisms, route-specific delivery strategies, stimuli-responsive and hierarchical systems, the selection of drug candidates with reference to physicochemical properties and the Biopharmaceutics Classification System, and applications in tissue engineering and wound care. Finally, clinically approved products and the main translational barriers, namely mechanical fragility, burst release, residual reagents, sterilization, batch-to-batch variability and regulatory classification, are critically evaluated to identify realistic routes towards next-generation, clinically useful hydrogel dosage forms.

paper_title: Machine Learning for the Design of Foundations on Rock Masses: A Critical Review of Data, Validation and Evidence Gaps
paper_abstract: Machine-learning (ML) models are increasingly proposed for the bearing capacity of foundations on rock masses, but the evidence for design use has not been appraised for rock foundations specifically. This narrative critical review links the mechanics of foundations on Hoek–Brown rock masses to an appraisal of the ML studies that target them. Of 275 unique Scopus and Web of Science records screened by one reviewer, 48 addressed ML for foundations on rock (full texts read for 11); 21 studies are tabulated with their data origin, size and validation. The review is not systematic. Numerical data sets contain 80 to 5,120 runs, whereas field or literature-compiled data sets for rock-socketed piles and shafts contain 96–200 records. Sample counts and inputs recur across studies. One study generated Gaussian-noise records from its full 136-shaft set and then split the combined set 85/15; three studies tested on the same measured shafts without stating overlap with the training database, the latest using qu as an input although the target is Nσ = qu/σci. A three-level validation hierarchy is adapted to rock foundations. An illustrative synthetic experiment, not a bearing-capacity model, shows that row-wise random cross-validation of project-structured data can give R² ≈ 0.996, whereas grouped cross-validation gives 0.68 ± 0.14. An error of ±5 units in the Geological Strength Index changes the Hoek–Brown constant s by factors of 1.74 and 0.57. Within the sources examined, ML serves mainly as a surrogate for numerical solvers; independent generalization and field validity have largely not been demonstrated.

paper_title: Sustainability Objectives in Polymer Machine Learning: A Critical Review of Integration, Reliability, and Evidence Gaps
paper_abstract: Machine learning (ML) is increasingly applied to polymers described as sustainable, yet sustainability may enter a workflow as material identity rather than as an explicit computational objective. This critical review combines narrative interpretation with a structured evidence analysis of a fixed analytical sample of 49 studies published from 2022 to 2026. It is a non-systematic review and does not claim exhaustive coverage; all numerical frequencies refer only to the analysed sample. Across four objective families—functional/material performance, end-of-life, hazard/ecotoxicity, and life-cycle impact—performance was modelled in-loop in 43/49 studies, compared with 14/49 for end-of-life and 3/49 for life-cycle impact; none of the 49 sampled studies modelled hazard/ecotoxicity in-loop. Ten studies modelled at least two objective families, and 8/10 used formal cross-family joint optimisation. Formal multi-objective optimisation appeared in 15 studies, but none of these 15 reported qualifying out-of-distribution (OOD) or grouped testing, explicit extrapolation testing, external-dataset validation, or applicability-domain analysis. Within the analytical sample, 5 of 15 possible non-empty objective combinations were occupied. These sample-level patterns suggest that optimisation sophistication has advanced faster than multidimensional sustainability integration and explicit validity assessment. Future polymer-ML workflows should state which sustainability endpoints are computationally represented, integrate validated non-performance objectives where data permit, and accompany candidate-space expansion with explicit evidence on uncertainty, generalisation, or applicability domains.

paper_title: Multi‑Medium Coupled Corrosion, Service‑Boundary Evolution and Integrity Management of Downhole Tubulars in High‑Sour Gas Fields: A Review
paper_abstract: Downhole tubulars in high-sour gas fields operate under extremely harsh conditions rarely seen in other industrial scenarios. With H2S partial pressures exceeding 1 MPa, Cl- concentrations reaching 2×105 mg·L-1 and frequent elemental sulfur deposition, the synergistic action of these corrosive species drives corrosion rates and cracking susceptibilities far beyond predictions from conventional single-medium tests. Based on field experience from China’s major high-sour gas blocks and extensive published literature, this review maps the operating window onto a three-dimensional service-boundary space defined by H2S partial pressure, temperature and Cl- concentration, and illustrates how temperature-dependent reaction pathways of elemental sulfur significantly shrink the valid service window of tubular materials. It clarifies the chained-evolution law among mass-loss, localized-defect and environment-assisted cracking failures, revealing that abrupt tubular failures typically occur after material service boundaries are exceeded. Five typical tubular material systems are compared regarding cost, mechanical performance and corrosion resistance. Advances in corrosion inhibitors, surface coatings and localized monitoring are reviewed, a closed-loop integrity-management framework for life-extension decision-making is proposed, and key technical bottlenecks for super-deep wells and emerging scenarios including CCUS, geothermal exploitation and underground hydrogen storage are highlighted.

paper_title: Management Accounting Practices and Organisational Performance Management in Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises in Soweto: A Systematic Review
paper_abstract: Introduction: Management accounting practices, including costing, budgeting, performance measurement, decision support and accounting information systems, are frequently linked with improved SME performance. However, the supplied evidence also indicates that benefits depend on organisational capability, information quality, management commitment, participation and implementation conditions. Direct evidence from SMEs located specifically in Soweto is absent from the supplied synthesis. Methods: The researcher-selected databases and information sources were Google Scholar and ERIC. The eligibility protocol restricted publication years to from 2020. The exact calendar date of search execution was not recorded in the verified identification provenance; this is distinct from the publication-year eligibility range. Google Scholar and ERIC were the researcher-selected information sources. The eligibility period was from 2020, while the search execution date was not recorded. Results: Costing, budgeting and performance evaluation were recurring practices. The dominant evidence pattern associated management accounting with improved financial, operational and managerial performance, although direct effects were inconsistent and mediated pathways were common. Budgeting, intellectual capital, performance measurement, decision quality and reporting quality acted as important mechanisms. Resource constraints, limited expertise, weak formalisation, inadequate information, cybersecurity concerns and limited risk-management capability restricted effective implementation. Participative, ethical and risk-aware use strengthened organisational relevance. Discussion/Conclusion: Management accounting practices appear generally beneficial when embedded in capable organisational systems rather than adopted as isolated tools. Nevertheless, conclusions for Soweto remain cautious because no supplied study directly examined Soweto SMEs. Future research should generate location-specific, longitudinal and methodologically transparent evidence focused on township, informal, micro and small-enterprise conditions.

paper_title: Modulating DNA Methylation in Mature Hair Cells to Mitigate Cisplatin-Induced Hearing Loss: A Review
paper_abstract: Cisplatin-induced hearing loss (CIHL) is a debilitating side effect in cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy. So far, epigenetic studies in the inner ear have largely focused on developmental biology to regenerate hair cells. In post-mitotic hair cells, on the other hand, DNA methylation regulates transcriptomic response to external stimuli. Adult mammalian hair cells are locked in the G0 phase, and passive demethylation via DNA replication does not occur under normal physiological conditions. However, external stimuli such as cisplatin can aberrantly upregulate DNMT methyltransferases (DNMTs), resulting in promoter methylation and silencing protective genes. From this angle, DNMTs modulation is an attractive therapeutic strategy to protect hearing during chemotherapy. Recent studies suggest that non-nucleoside inhibitors such as RG108 and natural polyphenolic compounds downregulate DNMTs, and at the same time, protect auditory cells. These compounds function via the inhibition of the DNMT catalytic site but can also act through downregulating DNMT1 and DNMT3A/B at mRNA and protein levels. Polyphenols are also antioxidants, decreasing reactive oxygen species, thereby increasing cell survival. Furthermore, it is suggested that upregulating TET-mediated active demethylation can be another angle to modify DNA methylation in cancer and CIHL models. However, functional DNA methylation should be distinguished from non-functional, passenger DNA methylation to elucidate the compounds’ otoprotective effects. In addition, the candidate compounds should not interfere with cisplatin’s antitumor effect. In this review, we investigate the relationship between DNA methylation and CIHL in the post-mitotic inner ear and evaluate the therapeutic potential of candidate DNMT inhibitors.

paper_title: Point-of-Care Diagnostics for Skin Neglected Tropical Diseases: A Systematic Review of Diagnostic Performance and Implementation Readiness
paper_abstract: Background: Point-of-care (POC) diagnostics could improve timely diagnosis of skin neglected tropical diseases (skin NTDs) in settings with limited access to laboratory services. However, evidence on their diagnostic performance, operational feasibility and readiness for decentralized implementation remains fragmented. Methods: We systematically searched PubMed, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and grey literature sources for studies evaluating POC diagnostic technologies for skin NTDs. Diagnostic performance, evidence maturity and operational characteristics were synthesized narratively because of heterogeneity across technologies, populations, reference standards, and reported outcomes. Diagnostic-accuracy studies were assessed using the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2 (QUADAS-2). Results: A short summary of the article’s main findings. Conclusions: POC diagnostics for skin NTDs show promising technological development but uneven evidence of maturity. Molecular technologies have generally progressed further in analytical development than in clinical and field validation, while simpler rapid tests have greater field experience but variable performance. Future research should prioritize prospective clinical and implementation-focused evaluation of complete diagnostic workflows in representative endemic settings.

paper_title: Buckling Behaviour and Design Assessment of Steel Square Hollow Section Columns: A Critical Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Steel square hollow section (SHS) columns may fail by local wall buckling, global flexural buckling, or interaction between these mechanisms. This narrative review examines the relationship between instability mechanisms, experimental evidence, numerical modelling and resistance assessment for steel SHS columns under compression. Particular attention is given to the distinction between cross-section and member slenderness, the influence of fabrication, residual stresses and geometric imperfections, and the transferability of findings among conventional, high-strength and stainless steels. Eurocode-based effective-section methods and the Direct Strength Method are discussed as resistance-prediction approaches, while finite element analysis is considered as a modelling framework whose reliability depends on validation and input assumptions. Evidence for perforated members and elevated-temperature conditions is addressed separately to avoid extrapolation beyond the investigated configurations. A bibliometric analysis of publications from 2000 to 2026 is used to identify research trends, influential sources and emerging topics. The review highlights the need for traceable experimental databases, transparent modelling of local and global imperfections, and matched comparisons of resistance predictions. Rather than claiming universal deficiencies in existing methods, it proposes a structured framework for identifying the geometrical and material domains in which further calibration of design provisions is justified.

paper_title: Inferring Business Relationships Between Autonomous Systems: A Survey of Evidence, Models, Algorithms, and Validation
paper_abstract: Business relationships between autonomous systems shape the routes that networks export and prefer. Public routing data expose these decisions incompletely, while commercial contracts usually remain private. Researchers therefore infer relationships from observed paths, routing attributes, registries, and network structure. This survey examines the literature within a 1996–2026 review window and separates five targets that are often conflated: link existence, relationship class, organizational ownership, routing policy, and financial settlement. We trace methods from hierarchy heuristics and combinatorial optimization to probabilistic inference, representation learning, and graph learning. We also examine multilateral peering, partial transit, hybrid relationships, and manipulation of inference inputs. Our central synthesis is that an inferred label is meaningful only together with its scope, evidence, and validation population. Path consistency does not establish commercial correctness, agreement with an inferred dataset does not establish independent accuracy, and a shared owner does not establish a routing adjacency. We develop a common problem formulation, compare the assumptions of representative methods, audit the interpretation of published results, and propose an evaluation protocol that separates observation bias, label dependence, temporal change, and downstream error costs. The resulting research agenda prioritizes scoped relationship representations, independent validation, calibrated uncertainty, and accountable inference pipelines.

paper_title: Complications from Port-a-Cath System Implantation in Adults Between 2018 and 2025: A Single-Center Restrospective Observational Review
paper_abstract: Purpose: Implantable venous ports provide durable intravenous access but carry inherent risks. This study aimed to characterise portacath complication rates at our institution over eight years and to assess the impact of the COVID19 pandemic. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 344 consecutive patients who underwent port placement at the University of Pécs between 1 March 2018 and 29 November 2025. Data collected included demographics, underlying malignancy, comorbidities, immunocompromise and timing of implantation relative to chemotherapy. Complications were recorded and classified as acute or delayed. Associations between patient factors and complications were analysed using descriptive statistics and χ2 tests. Results: Overall, 31 of 344 ports developed complications, resulting in a complication rate of 9.25%. Infections (8.95%) and skin breakdown or decubitus ulcers (7.63%) were the most common events, while mechanical failure, catheter malposition, and pneumothorax occurred only rarely. Complication rates did not differ significantly by age, sex, comorbidities, immunocompromised status, timing of implantation or pandemic period. Conclusions: At our centre, ultrasound-guided portacath implantation was associated with a low complication rate, even during the COVID19 pandemic. Complications were primarily infectious or cutaneous and showed no clear association with demographic variables or timing of insertion. Rigorous aseptic technique, meticulous surgical placement and comprehensive patient education are essential to minimise adverse events.

paper_title: A Scientometric Review of Construction Health, Safety and Wellbeing: Trends, Gaps, Regulation and Organisational Structures
paper_abstract: The construction industry has always been lagging behind with the development con-cerning worker health, safety and well-being due to an inherently anarchic nature and a non-conformal culture. However, less effort has been put toward reviewing these critical areas along with newly arising issues, gaps and areas of further research for its better implementation to achieve enhanced regulatory compliance. This study executed the scientometric review to gauge the level of research productivity and knowledge on Construction Industry Occupational Health Safety and Welfare between 1952 and 2025 with the help of the PRISMA research design. The efforts are concentrated through co-authorships and co-occurring keyword and co-citation analyses, as well as via cross-referencing with respective countries and years of publication, which will sketch out the key development of this discipline. Revealing critically important analysis through quantitative methods of scientometric mapping for several bibliographic rec-ords, 878 extracted from the Scopus database. Nonetheless, the Safety Science journal has been the main repository of publications. The study intended to share a broad exami-nation of the environmental exposure scenario and preliminary advancements on health and safety practices in the construction industry. New linkages and future trends in construction-related occupation were alluded to in this research. This work serves a significant reference of good intellectual intervention direction and policy to improve worker safety and health in the construction industry. The study also came up with a proposed framework on occupational health, safety, and wellbeing within the con-struction industry and focused on compliance with regulations and organizational structures.

paper_title: Motion Capture Technologies in Rehabilitation: A Critical Review of Accuracy, Clinical Validity, and Applicability
paper_abstract: Biomechanical analysis of human movement supports rehabilitation decisions requiring objective and reproducible measurements. However, motion capture technologies are commonly evaluated as separate technological families. This critical review compares marker-based optoelectronic, markerless, inertial, and hybrid systems in terms of accuracy, clinical validity, reliability, and implementation feasibility, and proposes methodological criteria for future validation studies. Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, and IEEE Xplore were searched, supplemented by forward and backward citation searching from eight seed studies. The selection process was reported using a PRISMA 2020 flow diagram. No protocol was registered, and no formal risk-of-bias assessment was conducted. Eligible studies involved human participants in clinical, rehabilitation, or functional assessment settings and reported quantitative performance metrics. Evidence was synthesized by technological family and application scenario. Ninety-six documents were included. Marker-based systems provided the highest accuracy for joint kinematics, whereas markerless and inertial systems showed comparable validity for spatiotemporal variables and global movement characterization. However, errors in specific joint angles remained above clinically desirable thresholds. Calibration procedures and assessment duration substantially influenced performance. No technology was universally superior. Therefore, selection should be made by variable, task and population, using explicit validation criteria.

paper_title: Large Language Models for Cybersecurity: A Survey of Data, Training, Models, Agent Systems, Evaluation, and Applications
paper_abstract: Advances in language understanding, code reasoning, and tool use are enabling cybersecurity agents to progress from question answering and single-step analysis to vulnerability research, incident investigation, and multistage task execution. These tasks require models to gather information, adapt their strategies, and verify results through sustained interaction, making capability development increasingly dependent on data, training, and runtime mechanisms. This survey examines research on Large Language Models (LLMs) for cybersecurity across six dimensions: data, training, models, agent systems, evaluation, and applications. We first examine how security corpora, instruction examples, interaction trajectories, and preference data are constructed, and how executable environments support training and validation. We then compare domain-adaptive continued pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization, agentic reinforcement learning, and distillation; analyze the capabilities of security-specialized and general-purpose models; and review mechanisms for planning, tool use, memory management, coordination, and verification. Drawing on representative benchmarks and experimental results, we assess progress and identify major bottlenecks across applications in threat intelligence, vulnerability analysis and remediation, malware analysis, security operations, and digital forensics. Based on this systematic review and analysis, we argue that cybersecurity LLMs are progressing from acquiring domain knowledge to learning how to perform interactive tasks. High-quality security data supports domain learning and task-specific supervision. Executable environments extend this training to multistep analysis and tool use, with outcome feedback guiding strategy refinement. Task quality and cost depend on both the model and its harness: the model reasons and selects actions, while the harness organizes information, tools, and execution state. Improvements in vulnerability discovery and threat analysis must also support effective remediation and timely response to yield lasting security benefits. Future research should develop agentic training and model–harness co-optimization methods that use validated attack–defense interactions to support continual improvement. Learning from operational tasks could further extend model capabilities and their contribution to cybersecurity practice.

paper_title: Japanese Surveys of the Chinese Herpetofauna During the Japanese Invasion of China
paper_abstract: During the Japanese invasion of China (1894 - 1945), the Japanese carried out compre-hensive surveys of natural resources in China, including amphibians and reptiles that this article focuses on. The surveys of herpetofauna were conducted by dozens of Japanese scholars from about a dozen Japanese universities and academic institutions. The surveys’ results were presented in the books, monograph, reports, articles, and lectures at the time. Now, about 100 years later, with the gradual release of these historical documents, it is possible to conduct research on the history of colonial science during the Japanese invasion of China. A total of 93 species, comprising 25 amphibians (4 Caudata + 21 Anura) and 68 reptiles (2 Crocodylia + 7 Testudines + 15 Lacertilia + 44 Serpentes), were discovered and recorded in those original documents. These 93 species account for 17.2% of the 540 species (168 amphibians + 372 reptiles) recorded in China before 1945, and the proportions of amphibians and reptiles were 14.9% (25/168) and 18.3% (68/372) respectively. In the present study, those names of species from approximately 100 years ago and their rec-orded distribution locations in the historical documents were listed and compared with their current scientific names and distribution areas. We also discussed the changes in taxonomy and natural history information of some species. This article aims to provide a new perspective for understanding the colonial nature of Japanese scientific expeditions to China and some basic information of the science history studies of Chinese herpetology.

paper_title: Flavor Modulation Strategies for Sodium Reduction in Processed Foods: A Review
paper_abstract: Sodium chloride occupies a functional position in processed foods that a simple subtraction cannot easily replace: it is simultaneously a tastant, a preservative, a texture modifier, and — less obviously — a modulator of other flavors, suppressing bitterness and amplifying sweetness and umami. Population-level sodium intake nonetheless remains roughly double recommended levels in most industrialized countries, and processed and away-from-home foods account for the large majority of that intake, which has made flavor-preserving sodium reduction one of the more persistent problems in food product development. This review synthesizes recent literature on strategies that address the flavor consequence of sodium removal specifically, organized around five mechanistic categories: taste-receptor-level substitution (potassium and mineral salts, plant- and marine-derived alternatives), chemosensory flavor enhancement (umami compounds, yeast-derived and fermentation-derived salty/umami peptides, bitter blockers), cross-modal and multisensory perception strategies (odor-induced saltiness enhancement, herb and spice seasoning, taste-taste and taste-texture interactions), physical and structural engineering of salt and food matrices (crystal morphology, particle size reduction, inhomogeneous spatial distribution, encapsulation), and processing-assisted approaches (high-pressure processing, ultrasound). Across food categories — meat, bread and bakery, cheese, and snacks — the evidence indicates that no single strategy reliably sustains more than a 20–30% sodium reduction without a perceptible flavor penalty, but combinations of mechanistically distinct strategies (e.g., a potassium-based substitute plus a bitterness-masking polysaccharide plus a savory aroma) can compound their effects to reach 50% or more. The review also considers the industrial and regulatory context shaping which of these strategies actually reach the shelf, since global sodium reduction remains off-track against the World Health Organization's 2025 target despite two decades of reformulation research. It closes by identifying where the evidence base is thin — chiefly the durability of consumer acceptance over repeated exposure, and the scalability of some promising laboratory-stage technologies — and where near-term industrial opportunity is greatest.

paper_title: Building Emergency Management Capacity Through Nursing Student Integration: A Literature and Experiential Review
paper_abstract: The growing frequency of disasters, from hurricanes to pandemics, has strained emergency management (EM) systems, highlighting the need for an expanded workforce. Nursing students, with their clinical expertise and enthusiasm for practical experience, offer a valuable resource to enhance community resilience. This literature review synthesizes 10 peer-reviewed studies from 2015 to 2025 to explore strategies for integrating nursing students into EM programs, particularly for universities without established programs. From the perspective of a lifelong public health responder now teaching nursing students, the review identifies simulation-based training, interprofessional collaborations, community partnerships, and curriculum integration as key strategies documented in the literature, while offering some real-world individual experience. Outcomes of the strategies include improved student competencies, enhanced community preparedness, and increased professional development, though some challenges like training gaps and logistical complexities persist. Lessons learned are discussed as well as some practical steps for universities to take from scratch to achieve the title goal. Future research directions are suggested to evaluate long-term impacts and scalability, offering actionable insights, especially for educators.

paper_title: From Prediction to Thinking: A Review of Reasoning in Industrial Recommender System
paper_abstract: Thinking has become an increasingly visible theme in recommendation research, but the termcovers mechanisms with different purposes, computational costs, and evidential support. To ourknowledge, this work presents the first systematic review dedicated specifically to thinking andreasoning mechanisms in industrial recommender systems. We trace its development in orig-inal research involving major technology platforms, from behavioral prediction and semanticgrounding to explicit chain-of-thought, recommendation-specific post-training, latent reason-ing, and amortized reasoning services. We organize the literature along three complementaryaxes: what grounds an intermediate state, how that state is represented and consumed, andhow its usefulness is learned or verified. Twenty-five core reports involving Microsoft Research,Huawei, Shopee, Kuaishou, Tencent, Alibaba/Taobao, Meta, JD.com, Netflix, and Xiaohongshuare analyzed alongside historical foundations, search applications, and industrial alternatives.The evidence indicates that reasoning supervision, inference-time reasoning, and productionsystem improvements must be evaluated separately. Explicit thinking is not consistently supe-rior to direct prediction; compact or cached states can retain useful supervision while reducingserving cost; and reinforcement learning can optimize biased rewards as readily as useful recom-mendations. We distinguish company participation, proprietary-data evaluation, and random-ized online evidence, and propose an evaluation framework that combines predictive quality,intervention-based reasoning tests, serving eﬀiciency, and user utility. The resulting accounttreats thinking as a developing system capability whose value depends on grounding, feedback,and computation allocation.

paper_title: A Systematic Review of Social Determinants of Health in Harare, Dissecting the Affordability Dichotomy Between Private and Public Healthcare
paper_abstract: Introduction: Healthcare affordability in Harare is shaped by social and economic conditions, including income, employment, insurance status, medicine availability and household insecurity. Public care may offer lower entry costs than private care, but shortages, facility-level price variation and payment mechanisms can generate additional expenditure. Methods: The researcher-selected databases and information sources were Google Scholar, PubMed (MEDLINE) and ERIC. The eligibility protocol restricted publication years to 2020–2026. The exact calendar date of search execution was not recorded in the verified identification provenance; this is distinct from the publication-year eligibility range. Google Scholar, PubMed (MEDLINE) and ERIC were searched using a prespecified Boolean strategy for English-language studies published from 2020 to 2026. Results: The direct Harare evidence was concentrated in qualitative diabetes-care research. Public referral care was described as cheaper and more accessible to low-income and generally uninsured households, but local consultation fees, medicine shortages, transport and searching costs, cash co-payments, exchange-rate disadvantages and possible improper charging weakened effective affordability. Household economic insecurity constrained continuity of chronic disease treatment. Information about medicine sources was enabling, while digital infrastructure and network limitations constrained telehealth. Remittances were associated with greater use of private facilities in wider urban Zimbabwe evidence. Discussion/Conclusion: Affordability in Harare is relative and pathway-dependent rather than determined solely by sector. Public care can reduce initial financial barriers, yet system shortages and payment failures shift costs to households. Confidence is moderated by concentrated disease-specific evidence, thin direct comparison of private and public care, contextual transferability limits and incomplete.

paper_title: Panner: A Low-Cost, High-Recall Pre-Screening Module for Systematic Reviews
paper_abstract: Before a model can screen a citation, the review team must decide what satisfies each eligibility criterion and which combinations of findings justify exclusion. PANNER makes these decisions explicit through interactive protocol compilation. A host agent works with the team to turn the criteria into atomic signal questions, answer conditions and rules for combining the answers. After the team reviews and freezes the protocol, a calibrated decision model answers the questions for each citation, and a fixed rule engine derives the retain or exclude decision. Records are retained for further assessment whenever no exclusion rule is satisfied. Implemented as a local Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, PANNER preserves the source criteria, protocols, answers and run configurations for inspection and recomputation. In four worked examples, it screened 26,195 deduplicated citations and excluded 21,768 (83.1%), leaving 4,427 for downstream screening. All 67 supplied reference reports were retained; these records also informed protocol calibration. Jev screening cost US$3.39, with approximately US$0.54 in estimated agent compilation costs. The examples illustrate how an explicit screening protocol can guide inexpensive batch judgements and reduce the number of records requiring further assessment.

paper_title: Biocontainment Transport of Patients with High-Consequence Infectious Diseases: A Narrative Review and Integrated Operational Framework for Emergency Medical Systems
paper_abstract: Background/Objectives: The transport of patients with high-consequence infectious diseases (HCIDs) links biosafety science and emergency medicine. The 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease epidemic and the multinational Andes virus outbreak associated with an expedition cruise ship have renewed attention on how such patients are moved safely between the community, hospitals and high-level isolation units. This narrative review synthesises the international literature on biocontainment transport and integrates it into an operational framework for emergency medical systems. Methods: A structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus (to 10 October 2026), complemented by guidance from the World Health Organization, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and national authorities, was conducted and reported according to the SANRA scale. Evidence was organised across seven operational domains and combined with the operational experience of the Italian Red Cross biocontainment transport service. Results: Of 2432 records identified, 1485 unique records were screened. The literature is dominated by aeromedical case reports, technical evaluations and expert consensus, with few comparative studies. Recurrent findings concern device integrity and air quality within transport isolators, the risk of self-contamination during doffing, heat strain and communication limits imposed by personal protective equipment, decontamination of vehicles and isolators, the maintenance of team readiness during periods of low activity, and the psychological burden on patients and staff. These findings are integrated into a framework comprising a four-link containment chain, a seven-phase operational workflow, a three-tier complexity classification and a role-based responsibility matrix. Conclusions: Biocontainment transport is better understood as an integrated emergency system than as a device-centred intervention. The proposed framework is a structured, consensus-based reference for planning, training and quality assurance; its components require prospective evaluation.

paper_title: Machine Learning Meets Blockchain: A Domain-Oriented Review of Integration Mechanisms, Applications, and Open Challenges
paper_abstract: Blockchain and machine learning (ML) are combined in systems that must learn from multi-party data and keep a verifiable record of what was used and decided. This scoping-style review of a ranked sample covers seven domains: healthcare, finance, supply chain, energy, smart contracts, transportation and education. We searched Scopus and IEEE Xplore on 15 October 2026, ranked 5,195 candidate records, read 345 abstracts in rank order, coded a core corpus of 192 studies and read 38 in full. Federated learning is the most common method (93 of 192 core studies name it), and detection of fraud, intrusions and vulnerabilities is the most common task among the 38. None of the 38 reports a deployment, 24 report a measured ledger figure and two measure ledger energy. Ten use more than one privacy mechanism, and only two report accuracy with and without it. Attack tests are small, and one study tests a Sybil attacker. Studies differ too much to compare, so we do not rank domains. A ledger shows that a record has not changed, not that it was correct when written. The main gaps are realistic evaluation, shared benchmarks and reporting standards, and tested explanations for decisions made inside contracts.

paper_title: Major Revision, Minor Accountability: LLMs as Reviewers of Published Articles in Top-Tier Journals
paper_abstract: With the growth of scientific output, the peer review system is approaching a breaking point: reviewers are increasingly hard to secure, and turnaround times lengthen accordingly. LLM-assisted or LLM-generated peer review has been proposed as a remedy, but how such models would treat manuscripts already published in top-tier journals, the closest thing the current system has to a gold standard of scientific validity, is not known. Here we assembled a corpus of 200 articles, each released under a CC BY 4.0 license and published in 2026, from 20 general-science, life-science, and clinical-medicine journals including Nature, Science, and Cell, and asked four current LLMs (two proprietary, two open-weight) to produce independent peer-review reports of each one under a blinded protocol. Their decisions were overwhelmingly harsh and starkly inconsistent with each other: 605 of 800 reviews (75.6%) recommended major revision or rejection, but the rate at which any single model did so ranged from 17.5% to 100% (p < 0.001), disagreement on manuscripts that had, by construction, already survived real editorial review at the journals in question. When the same manuscripts were doctored with one deliberately planted, field-specific methodological or statistical flaw, detection rates varied from 17.0% to 60.5% across models (p < 0.001). Recommending revision for papers that had already passed editorial review (low specificity) while missing flaws deliberately placed in front of them (low sensitivity), these models produce output that should be read for what it is: an uneven, framing- and model-dependent signal.

paper_title: SurveyGraph: Generating Academic Surveys via Methods-Entity Knowledge Graphs
paper_abstract: Most automated survey generation systems retrieve papers as flat documents, limiting their ability to capture research structure. We present SurveyGraph, a framework built around a Methods-Entity Knowledge Graph (MEKG) encoding method-level follow-on, competition, and shared-resource relations. The graph supports core-paper discovery, retrieval, hybrid outlining, and evidence-gated narrative synthesis. We evaluate retrieval, semantic edges, citation grounding, collection coverage, and generation-stage components. In a controlled seven-method equal-budget benchmark, MEKG-anchored fusion balances recall and structural density, with an independent co-citation check. In a separate archived graph-native diagnostic, graph-aware retrieval nearly doubles recall over flat lexical baselines across eight runs (p = 0.004). A semantic evidence gate achieves AUC = 0.75. Audits of 160 generated sentences find 80.6% anchored-or-partial citation support. Human adjudication of 108 stratified semantic edges finds 68.5% supported-or-partial relations (binary-support Cohen's kappa = 0.64), with improves strongest (80.6%) and extends weakest (52.8%). A SurveyBench-facing collection probe reaches mean reference coverage of 0.521 across four topics with an eight-paper budget. Same-backend Qwen diagnostics on a 30-paper/74-relation graph show reduced organization signals when hybrid outlining is removed. Concurrent-system comparisons provide bounded context rather than matched-backend end-to-end evidence. The results position MEKG as an auditable structural layer for typed diagnostics, relation-specific filtering, and controlled survey generation. Code and artifacts: https://github.com/xzzvsxd/SurveyGraph.
comments: Accepted at EMNLP 2026 Findings. 34 pages including appendices

paper_title: Data-Driven Vision-Language Models for Remote Sensing: A Survey
paper_abstract: During the deep learning era, innovations in remote sensing (RS) vision models primarily focused on optimizing network architectures for specific tasks and conducting end-to-end training. However, with the advent of the Vision-Language Models (VLMs) era, constrained by substantial computational resource demands, the mainstream research paradigm has shifted towards adapting general-purpose VLMs using RS vertical domain data for fine-tuning, rather than modifying their core architectures. This transition marks a change in the innovation pathway from model-centric to data-centric. Despite the increasing importance of data, the academic community still lacks a systematic, data-centric survey to guide researchers in constructing high-quality RS vision-language datasets for various application scenarios and in conducting effective model fine-tuning and performance evaluation based on these datasets. To address this gap, this paper presents a systematic review of the development status of RS datasets tailored for VLMs. It further provides a comprehensive practical guide for RS researchers in the large model era, covering the entire pipeline from data construction to fine-tuning and evaluation. This paper aims to encourage the academic community to build more diverse and higher-quality vision-language datasets for specialized RS sub-fields. Ultimately, the goal is to converge these efforts into a comprehensive RS vision-language corpus that offers extensive task coverage and a wide geographical distribution, thereby laying a solid data foundation for advancing towards general artificial intelligence in RS.

paper_title: Future of Time Series Anomaly Detection: From Historical Review to Unified Outlook
paper_abstract: Time series anomaly detection (TSAD) is a foundational problem in data mining, aiming to identify observations that deviate significantly from nominal temporal patterns. Driven by escalating data volumes and application complexity, recent research has yielded diverse architectures, including diffusion models, state space models, and large language models (LLMs). However, existing surveys provide limited coverage of these emerging designs and lack a unified treatment of multivariate anomalies, cross-domain unified modeling, metric reliability, and contemporary evaluation challenges. To bridge these gaps, this survey delivers three core contributions: (1) We establish a refined anomaly categorization and a structured taxonomy of paradigms reflecting modern advances, comparing detection mechanisms and charting developmental trajectories across paradigms. (2) We provide an extensive analysis of evaluation methodologies and conduct comprehensive experiments to assess metric fidelity, complemented by an open-source benchmark repository encompassing algorithms, datasets, and evaluation tools. (3) We outline key open challenges, offering forward-looking perspectives on dynamic thresholding, model interpretability, zero-shot transfer, multi-modal alignment, and foundational models for time series. By addressing existing theoretical and empirical limitations, this survey establishes a coherent framework to guide future TSAD research and practical deployments.
comments: 18 pages, 5 figures, 4 tables. Accepted by IEEE Transactions on Artificial Intelligence. DOI: 10.1109/TAI.2026.3746935

paper_title: Uncertainty Quantification for Financial Foundation Models: A Survey
paper_abstract: Financial foundation models increasingly support workflows spanning financial question answering, disclosure analysis, forecasting, and decision-making. In these settings, uncertainty may concern whether evidence is valid and available at the relevant time, whether an interpretation is justified, which outcomes remain plausible, or which action is preferred under costs and risk constraints. Because these objects arise at different points in a workflow, uncertainty cannot be reduced to confidence in a final output. We introduce a source-aware framework that distinguishes six sources of uncertainty across evidence and context, model and inference, and outcome and action, while treating agentic workflows as the execution layer through which uncertainty can propagate, change form, or be reduced. We develop a mechanism-based taxonomy grounded in how methods construct or verify uncertainty and reliability representations, and use it to assess their applicability across financial task domains. We further map finance-specific empirical studies across the taxonomy and task domains to characterize the current research landscape. Our analysis shows that most reviewed studies address uncertainty in individual parts of financial workflows, with limited work connecting evidence and reasoning reliability to downstream prediction and constrained action. By connecting where uncertainty arises, how it is represented, and how it bears on downstream decisions, this survey provides a unified foundation for studying and evaluating uncertainty in financial foundation models.
comments: Accepted at the 7th ACM International Conference on AI in Finance (ICAIF 2026). 8 pages

paper_title: Recursive Self Improvement for Embodied Agents—A Survey of Foundations Mechanisms Harnesses and Evaluation
paper_abstract: Embodied foundation models have expanded the range of instructions, observations, and actions that robots can process. Autonomy in execution, however, does not automatically provide autonomy in improvement. Robots must still diagnose failures, acquire useful experience, select interventions, and determine whether accepted changes improve future performance. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) connects these activities through persistent feedback and inheritance, with the stronger objective of improving the mechanisms that produce subsequent improvements. This survey distinguishes within-episode correction, persistent self-improvement, successive version inheritance, and meta-level improvement. It connects large-model learning, sequential agency, and RSI theory, and compares general agent harnesses with their embodied counterparts. It develops a four-axis framework covering improvement targets, update mechanisms, autonomy over improvement decisions, and evidence conditions. Using this framework, we examine reflection and knowledge revision, executable-program evolution, adaptive experience acquisition, parameter learning, world-model revision, and cross-layer intervention selection. We compare representative systems while retaining their assumptions about feedback, validation, transfer, and cost. We also review benchmarks and associated datasets for manipulation, long-horizon decision making, memory, and world modeling, separating pretraining data, improvement experience, candidate validation, and final evaluation. Existing results support several forms of component-level and system-level improvement, but capability gains, improvement autonomy, and demonstrated recursive gains require different evidence. We identify failure attribution, reliable feedback, physical reset, competence preservation, and independent evaluation of revised improvers as central research priorities.

paper_title: Predictable Information in Galaxy Rotation-Curve Discrepancies: Relocation to Independent, More Distant Surveys
paper_abstract: The predictive organization previously identified in SPARC galaxy rotation-curve discrepancies [1] is tested here across a substantially larger and more distant population. We use 1,387 galaxies drawn from four independently acquired PROBES source surveys. SPARC is used only to help establish the stellar-disk normalization and an empirical radial gas-velocity reconstruction. For each galaxy we define the signed squared-velocity discrepancy, ΔV²(r) = Vobs²(r) − Vbar²(r), characterize its radial structure, and test whether population relationships learned from other galaxies predict the withheld galaxy. Strict leave-one-galaxy-out prediction gives a velocity RMSE of 47.34 km s⁻¹, compared with 50.86 km s⁻¹ for a population-average residual control, a 6.92% reduction across 75,722 held-out radial predictions. Each of the four constituent surveys independently shows positive error reduction. A leave-one-survey-out test, training on three surveys and predicting the fourth, gives a pooled 7.20% gain; the SCII survey is statistically unresolved. In survey-stratified grouped withholding, the gain remains 6.81% even when approximately half of the 1,387 galaxies are excluded from model construction. The composite sample has a median distance of 88.7 Mpc, approximately 5.2 times that of the original SPARC population. These results show that the same galaxy-level predictive architecture identified in SPARC can be recovered independently in a much larger, more distant, and less homogeneous four-survey population, even though its baryonic baseline must be reconstructed rather than supplied directly. Fixed SPARC coefficients expectedly do not transfer unchanged to PROBES, and direct near-to-far prediction is not established due to survey heterogeneity. Against a training-fitted radial-acceleration relation (RAR), the PRIM (Predictive Residual Informational Mapping) to PROBES is competitive overall but not uniformly superior; its physical origin remains unresolved.

paper_title: Erectile Dysfunction among Male University Students in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso: A Cross-Sectional Survey of Prevalence, Associated Factors, and Help-Seeking
paper_abstract: Background: Data on erectile dysfunction (ED) in young African men are scarce. We estimated ED prevalence among male university students in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, and examined associated factors, psychosocial impact, and help-seeking. Methods: In this cross-sectional online survey (January-July 2026), male students aged 18-30 years at Joseph Ki-Zerbo University completed an anonymous questionnaire. The five-item International Index of Erectile Function (IIEF-5) was scored in men who had attempted intercourse in the previous four weeks, with ED defined as a score of 21 or less. Associated factors were examined by multivariable logistic regression. Results: Of 696 respondents (mean age 24.1 ± 3.2 years), 476 were evaluable. ED was present in 240 (50.4%; 95% CI 45.9-54.9); it was mild in 151 and moderate or severe in 20. Self-reported depression (adjusted odds ratio 4.04; 95% CI 1.10-14.88) and other chronic conditions (1.87; 1.11-3.15) were independently associated with ED; age, alcohol, and tobacco use were not. Among men with ED, 66.5% reported interference with academic work, and only 11.9% of those acknowledging a problem had consulted a health professional. Shame was the most cited barrier (61.4%). Conclusions: Mostly mild ED was common in this sample and was linked to depression and chronic illness rather than lifestyle. Campus services should offer confidential sexual and mental health screening.
paper_authors: Yameogo Clotaire Alexis Marie Kiemdiba Donega

paper_title: Cold-Start and Skill-Aware Job Recommender Systems: A Scoping Review of Data, Models, and Evaluation Evidence
paper_abstract: Job recommender systems support applicant–vacancy matching, but their reliability is uncertain when users or jobs are new, or information is sparse. This scoping review maps cold-start and skill-aware job recommendations, emphasizing early-career populations. Following PRISMA-ScR, we searched Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and EBSCO for studies published from 2010 to 2026. We screened 1,891 unique records, assessed 155 full texts, and included 76 primary studies. Fifty-eight studies specified at least one cold-start scenario, and 48 directly concerned early-career populations. Information representations, recommendation architectures, and evaluation designs were heterogeneous. Most importantly, none of the five field comparisons with reported real-world outcomes directly evaluated an early-career cohort. The available evidence therefore supports task- and dataset-specific performance claims more strongly than claims of employment benefit for first-time or early-career job seekers. We propose a six-stage evaluation framework connecting population definition, cold-start construction, information assessment, controlled offline comparison, human assessment, and prospective outcomes.

paper_title: AI-Enabled Smart and Precision Agriculture: Smart Sensors, IoT, Deep Learning, Computer Vision, and Decision Support: A Comprehensive Survey
paper_abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated with smart sensors, Internet of Things (IoT) networks, machine learning, deep learning, and computer vision to support site-specific agricultural management. However, strong performance on computational benchmarks does not necessarily translate into reliable decisions, effective field interventions, or measurable improvements in agricultural productivity and resource efficiency. This comprehensive narrative survey critically synthesizes advances in agricultural sensing, IoT architectures, data processing, multimodal sensor fusion, predictive modeling, computer vision, decision optimization, and automated actuation. Particular emphasis is placed on the relationships between measurement reliability, model generalization, decision feasibility, intervention accuracy, and verified agricultural outcomes. The reviewed literature demonstrates promising capabilities in crop monitoring, yield prediction, disease and weed recognition, precision irrigation, and selected automated operations. Nevertheless, heterogeneous evaluation protocols, limited independent field validation, sensor calibration challenges, distribution shifts, interoperability barriers, and deployment costs constrain operational reliability and generalizability. To address these interconnected challenges, the survey proposes a literature-informed reference architecture linking agricultural observations, data integration, AI inference, constrained decision-making, physical interventions, and outcome feedback, supported by uncertainty assessment, human oversight, and cross-layer assurance. The proposed architecture is conceptual and has not been empirically validated. Future research priorities include reproducible field evaluations, representative agricultural datasets, uncertainty-aware and explainable AI, resource-efficient computing, interoperable infrastructures, and economically inclusive deployment. The review concludes that the practical value of AI-enabled precision agriculture should be evaluated through reliable interventions, sustainable resource utilization, and demonstrated agricultural outcomes rather than predictive performance alone.

paper_title: A Task-Centric Survey of Long-Document Visual Question Answering: Taxonomy, Evolution, and Future Directions
paper_abstract: Visual document understanding is essential for acquiring knowledge from visually rich documents and is attracting growing research interest. Existing surveys emphasize architectures or technical approaches, with limited attention to how task bottlenecks shape technical choices and research priorities. We present a task-centric survey that decomposes long-document visual question answering (VQA) into four components: document parsing, evidence organization and retrieval, generator organization and learning, and evaluation. For each, we develop a fine-grained taxonomy and trace motivations, technical responses, and cross-component connections. We focus on explicit retrieval while covering direct reading. Our temporal analysis traces expanding priorities from multimodal content understanding to sufficient, high-fidelity evidence acquisition and sustained evidence management. We outline future directions in evidence sufficiency, verifiable and correctable understanding, and budget-aware coordination, with an outlook on continual document understanding.

paper_title: A Survey on Side-Tuning for Foundation Models
paper_abstract: The adaptation cost of parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) depends on trainable parameters, activation storage, and the computations required for optimization. Methods such as LoRA and adapters may still require backward computation through frozen backbone operations and retention or recomputation of intermediate activations. Side-tuning places trainable adaptation modules outside the backbone, creating opportunities to reduce this cost through different connections to the backbone gradient graph. This survey presents a topology- and deployment-aware study of side-tuning for foundation models and proposes a graph-topological definition with three categories: graph-coupled side-tuning, in which an external side branch remains coupled to backbone gradients; mixed side-tuning, in which a detached side path re-enters a later layer of the same backbone; and detached side-tuning, in which an external trainable network consumes frozen backbone representations through a stop-gradient interface and computes task-specific gradients entirely outside the backbone. We review a curated cross-domain corpus spanning natural language processing, computer vision, multimodal learning, recommendation, and relevant methodological precursors, while examining information retrieval as an emerging deployment setting. The literature is organized along three axes: gradient topology, feature interface, and deployment regime. We derive a resource model that accounts for backward activations, online feature production, and cached representations, and use it to develop design guidelines and reporting recommendations. This organization connects the training graph of each method to its resource requirements and the conditions under which its features can be reused.

paper_title: Primary Lung Cancer In Vitro Models and Patient-Derived Organoids from Minimally Invasive Procedures: A Review of Methods and Translational Potential
paper_abstract: Primary cultures and organoids from lung cancer patients preserve tumor heterogeneity and enable patient-specific functional testing. Their generation has relied largely on surgical resection, which most patients never undergo because their disease is diagnosed too late. This review examines whether minimally invasive sources, namely cryobiopsy, endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration, bronchoscopic biopsy, computed tomography (CT)-guided transthoracic needle biopsy, and malignant pleural effusion, can serve as alternatives. To compare outcomes across studies, we distinguish four endpoints: tissue adequacy, initial formation, long-term validated establishment, and molecular fidelity to the source tumor. Reported establishment rates from these sources range from 10% to over 80%, and some matched or exceeded surgical tissue within the same study. Yet these figures depend on how success is defined. In one cohort, organoids formed from 41% of specimens, but only 17% yielded verified tumor organoids. In another, cancer-associated fibroblasts dominated 46 of 51 cultures. Anatomical site, medium composition, and overgrowth by stromal or normal airway cells therefore explain outcomes better than acquisition route alone. Ex vivo drug responses have been linked to clinical outcomes, but prospective validation is lacking. Standardized multi-endpoint reporting and routine confirmation of molecular fidelity are needed before these models can guide therapy.

paper_title: From Perception Errors to Unsafe Actions: A Survey of Behavioral Safety in MLLM Agents
paper_abstract: Multimodal large language model (MLLM) agents connect perceptual inputs to tools and external actions, making safety a property of trajectories and retained state. This curated survey uses a constrained partially observable Markov decision process to organize six risk families: grounding failure, observation manipulation, miscalibrated authority, inference-time hijacking, unsafe commitment, and reusable-state corruption. We compare safeguards by mechanism, access requirements, and evidence scope, separating direct multimodal execution from transferred model-level and text-agent findings. The synthesis emphasizes image–text, GUI/web, and selected embodied settings; it is neither exhaustive nor independently coded. We distinguish response scores from executed violations and later-task reactivation, and propose containment and restoration outcomes for recovery evaluation. These distinctions motivate execution safeguards, calibrated autonomy, and integrity checks for reusable agent state.

paper_title: Increased Neck Circumference and Altered Cervical Fascial Mechanics: Rehabilitation Implications of a Six-System Coupling Framework for the Carotid Sheath—A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Background: Increased neck circumference is commonly viewed as a simple surrogate marker of upper-body adiposity and cardiometabolic risk. However, cervical fat accumulation simultaneously alters the mechanical load borne by the investing fascia, and reduced elastic buffering capacity may permit abnormal shear stress to be conducted through the deep cervical fascial network to the carotid sheath. The carotid sheath is an anatomical hub shared by the internal carotid artery, internal jugular vein, lymphatic vessels, glymphatic outflow pathways, cervical sympathetic trunk, and vagus nerve.Objective: To organize evidence from anatomical, epidemiological, imaging, and intervention studies within a testable integrative framework, to grade evidence maturity by node, and to propose a research agenda.Methods: This narrative review evaluates the “six-system coupling framework” as a testable integrative perspective rather than an established causal mechanism. Evidence maturity was graded by node using a custom five-tier scale. The core empirical gap was identified as the absence of simultaneous measurement of investing fascia elasticity, intra-sheath pressure, and intra-sheath functional markers in the same individual.Results: Anatomically, the investing fascia and the carotid sheath have a composite relationship that is partly loose and partly directly continuous. Focal absence and midline-crossing connections further increase the spatial heterogeneity of transmission, whereas the prevertebral fascia serves as an anatomical barrier and protective mechanical constraint around the sheath. Evidence is strongest at the arterial node, supported by longitudinal cohorts, vascular-bed specificity, and PIEZO1/2 molecular candidates, and is graded moderate-high. The venous node has human evidence of mechanical sensitivity but has not been replicated under fascial mechanical exposure, and is graded moderate-low. The autonomic node has human muscle sympathetic nerve activity (MSNA) associations and randomized controlled trial (RCT) evidence for heart rate variability (HRV), but the intervention was not neck-specific, and is graded moderate. The glymphatic node has only indirect human associations and animal mechanistic evidence, and is graded low.Conclusions: Neck circumference and fascial mechanical parameters should be incorporated into multisystem rehabilitation assessment and monitored as mediators linking superficial body load to deep structural function. For rehabilitation, entry-level weight reduction and effector-level autonomic modulation can serve as independent components; investing fascia-targeted interventions at the transmission-interface level are currently investigational only. Their status as an independent intervention target awaits clarification through longitudinal studies oriented toward mediation analysis and functional endpoints.

paper_title: Can Hidden Reasoning Stay Hidden? A Survey of Chain-of-Thought Extraction Attacks on Large Reasoning Models
paper_abstract: Providers of large reasoning models withhold the chain-of-thought (CoT) that their models generate, returning an answer, a short summary, and, in some APIs, an encrypted copy of the trace in order to prevent distillation and keep sensitive intermediate content private. Five studies published between March and September 2026 show how API clients can recover existing traces or obtain useful reasoning despite this restriction. This survey organizes that work at the level of threat models, mechanisms, and evaluation protocols. We formulate CoT extraction, compare the attackers that the studies assume, and group the attacks into three families according to how they obtain the trace: reconstruction from visible outputs, elicitation into a visible channel, and replay of the trace that the model has already produced. We then summarize how the attacks are evaluated, map the proposed defenses onto the families they address, and identify open problems. The surveyed evaluations establish that no single defense is effective across all three families, and comparing attacks requires a shared trace reference and separate measures of textual fidelity, task preservation, and downstream utility. We conclude by identifying several research gaps and open questions for future research.

paper_title: The Cenozoic East Rhodopean Low‐Sulfidation Gold‐Silver Metallogenic Province, SE Bulgaria—Synthesis of Existing Data: A Review
paper_abstract: The low-sulfidation silver-gold prospects in the Eastern Rhodope Mountains, SE Bulgaria, united in the East Rhodopean low-sulfidation gold-silver metallogenic province, contain a considerable precious-metal endowment for current and future mining. For the most promising prospects, geochronological, stratigraphical, biostratigraphical, structural, mineralogical, and stable-isotope data exist, but their origin remains not fully understood. In this paper, we review existing data on geodynamics, metamorphism, magmatism, and their geochronology in the Rhodope Crystalline Massif, as well as data on the geology, mineralogy, stable isotope geochemistry, and formation conditions of low-sulfidation gold deposits from the Eastern Rhodopes, SE Bulgaria. The aim is to provide a synopsis of the existing data to help one construct a new genetic model for this class of economic deposits. The main conclusions which can be drawn from the reviewed literature are the following: (i) geochronological and stratigraphic constraints clearly revealed older age of these de-posits than the local Late Eocene- Early Oligocene magmatism; (ii) there is isotop-ic evi-dence of meteoric origin of the fluids; (iii) there is a seismological evidence of slab rollback since Eocene to Late Miocene-Pliocene in the Rhodope realm, (iv) conveying role of the deeply penetrating detachment fault systems for hot uprising fluids is evidenced by hy-drothermal alteration and silicification, both strong in places; and (v) heating of mete-oric water in the area of high heat flux produced by the Cenozoic crustal extension and as-thenospheric mantle upwelling in the Eastern Rhodopes is seems to be a necessary condi-tion for the formation of these deposits.

paper_title: Quantum Image Encryption: A Comprehensive Review of Representations, Encryption Schemes, Security Evaluation and Open Challenges
paper_abstract: Quantum image encryption (QIE) loads a digital image into qubits and ciphers it with unitary circuits, usually keyed by chaotic maps, quantum walks or quantum random numbers. This review follows the field from an early geometric-transformation scheme (2013) to designs executed on 127-qubit IBM processors (2025). We organise the literature by image representation (FRQI, NEQR, amplitude encoding), confusion and diffusion mechanism, key source and validation level, and we compare recent schemes on entropy, NPCR, UACI, correlation and key space. Reported statistics sit close to their ideals almost everywhere; recent quantum-walk and chaos-based designs report NPCR of 99.6 to 99.97% and UACI of 33.5 to 33.9%, so these metrics no longer separate strong schemes from weak ones. Three gaps stand out. Most evidence comes from classical simulation. The secret usually sits in a classical key generator rather than in the quantum circuit. And loading an image into qubits, then reading it back, remains the main hardware bottleneck. Hybrid designs that distribute keys with BB84 and cipher the image classically offer the most deployable route today. We close with a research agenda: attack-based benchmarks, error-aware hardware validation, cheaper state preparation and explicit security definitions.

paper_title: Effectiveness and Clinical Use of Virtual Reality in Cognitive Behavioral Psychotherapy: A Focused Narrative Review of Randomized Controlled Trials
paper_abstract: Virtual Reality (VR) can provide a more convenient and wider accessibility of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) by allowing feared situations to be produced and repeated in a virtual reality space. VR-based CBT may be helpful to treat anxiety disorders and psychosis, as well as to address the avoidance and anxiety involved in some cases of Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD). This focused narrative review aims to summarize evidence available in public sources by 2026, and address the use of VR to treat anxiety disorders, psychosis, and OCD, as well as related conditions. Given the high social and economic burden related to psychosis and the role of avoidance, the preliminary results of a few randomized control trials (RCTs) using VR-based CBT indicate a potential to reduce symptoms and improve quality of life. A key challenge in psychotherapy is translating the practice simulated in a safe environment to the real world. Research is still needed to address this challenge. The goal of this review is to analyze RCTs and summarize the value of VR and psychotherapy integration by including results of qualitative and economic studies.

paper_title: Positioning MBSE System Architectures in the Agent Harness Towards Automated Product Development: A Scoping Review
paper_abstract: The automation of product development is increasingly enabled by agents, which extend large language models (LLMs) from requirements engineering to computer-aided engineering (CAE). An agent can be understood as an LLM embedded in a software harness that provides tools, memory, execution loops, and feedback channels. Model-based systems engineering (MBSE) maintains the system architecture and may therefore provide an important source of context and state for such agents. This scoping review investigates which artifacts provide context and maintain state in the reported approaches, and whether the MBSE system architecture is among them. A systematic search of arXiv, IEEE Xplore, Scopus, and Web of Science on 1 August 2026 covered three search areas: MBSE and agents, MBSE and CAE, and agents and CAE. Of 14 584 records published from 2022 onward, title and abstract screening retained 495, of which 329, available in full text, were classified along the dimensions of their search area. Screening and classification were carried out by an LLM under author-defined criteria and closed vocabularies, reported along the PRISMA-trAIce checklist, and every evidence passage was verified against the full text. The review positions the MBSE system architecture within the agent harness and identifies how far the literature supports this role.

paper_title: Buffalo Hump, Neck Circumference, and Stroke Risk: A Narrative Review from a Surface Landmark to an Untested Intervention Target
paper_abstract: Background: Buffalo hump is often oversimplified as localized fat accumulation, but its tissue composition is heterogeneous, and its clinical significance extends beyond cosmetic concerns. Neck circumference has accumulated relatively consistent evidence in cardiometabolic epidemiology, but most integrated analyses have used metabolic risk factors or metabolic syndrome as endpoints rather than hard endpoints such as stroke. Whether enlargement of the buffalo hump leads to an increase in neck circumference, and whether interventions that reduce the buffalo hump or neck circumference can translate into stroke prevention, remain unresolved.
