This narrative review examines the evidence linking buffalo hump and neck circumference to stroke risk and identifies structural gaps that currently preclude translation into prevention strategies.Methods: PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and the China National Knowledge Infrastructure were searched through March 2026 using terms for buffalo hump or dorsocervical fat, neck circumference, stroke or carotid atherosclerosis, and physical therapy or exercise. Population studies, intervention studies, mechanistic studies, and systematic reviews/meta-analyses reporting neck circumference, buffalo hump, carotid imaging, or stroke/cardiovascular endpoints were included. Case reports alone, narrative reviews without quantitative outcomes, and duplicate publications were excluded. After deduplication, title/abstract screening, and full-text assessment, 42 articles were included. As a narrative review, screening was performed by a single author without independent dual screening; selection bias cannot be excluded, and exhaustive retrieval according to systematic review standards is not claimed. Results: Buffalo hump is morphologically heterogeneous and frequently co-occurs with obesity and metabolic disorders. Increased neck circumference is associated with ischemic stroke and its subclinical precursor, independently of overall obesity. In a cohort of 3,009 patients with type 2 diabetes, high neck circumference was associated with an approximately 2.3-fold higher risk of a composite cardiovascular endpoint that included stroke; this estimate was not stroke-specific. The association was relatively robust in women in some East Asian cohorts; however, a cohort using the same cutoffs reported stronger predictive performance in men, and negative results from the Jackson Heart Study and the Framingham Offspring Cohort indicate that the direction and presence of the association are not uniform across populations. Pericarotid fat density and perivascular adipose tissue attenuation show incremental predictive signals beyond plaque burden in some studies, but this incremental value has not been consistently quantified, and their quantitative relationship with neck circumference has not been established. Surgical debulking, diet, physical therapy, and exercise have preliminary evidence, but none has reported postintervention neck circumference change in relation to stroke endpoints. Forward head posture remains an untested candidate pathway. Conclusions: The existing evidence supports treating buffalo hump and neck circumference as surface markers of stroke risk and potential intermediate targets, but it is still insufficient to support the clinical conclusion that treating or reducing buffalo hump, or lowering neck circumference, can prevent stroke. Concurrent collection of neck circumference, buffalo hump subtype, carotid imaging parameters, obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) severity, atrial fibrillation, forward head posture parameters, and stroke endpoints, together with systematic tracking of postintervention neck circumference trajectories, may translate the current descriptive associations into testable prevention hypotheses.

paper_title: Cyberattack Dataset Engineering and Benchmarking for Realistic Intrusion Detection: A Survey
paper_abstract: Intrusion detection research depends on datasets. However, dataset design is often treated as secondary to model selection. In this survey, we examine cyberattack dataset engineering and benchmarking for realistic intrusion detection system (IDS) evaluation. Specifically, we review dataset releases, benchmark critiques, and domain-specific detection studies that cover general-purpose network benchmarks, Android spyware, multi-step and APT-inspired attacks including SUNBURST, smart-grid injection, SNMP-MIB and DDoS monitoring, IoT botnets, phishing, streaming traffic, and GAN-based synthetic attack data. We argue that dataset realism must be judged through collection context, attack procedure, benign behaviour, labeling, feature extraction, temporal splitting, privacy, reproducibility, and benchmark saturation, rather than through dataset size or reported accuracy. To this end, we position the survey against prior IDS and dataset reviews, introduce a six-dimensional dataset-centred taxonomy (attack environment, data representation, collection method, label strategy, evaluation protocol, and threat model), compare seven dataset families, and consolidate an evaluation protocol that covers split policy, leakage checks, baselines, metrics, and dataset documentation. We conclude that next-generation IDS datasets should be released with dataset cards, scenario cards, leakage reports, baseline scripts, chronological and holdout splits, adversarial and zero-day partitions, and explicit limitations. This shift would make IDS results more comparable, make inflated performance claims easier to detect, and support realistic evaluation for IoT, 5G, smart grids, Android malware, phishing, and APT-inspired attacks.

paper_title: From Earth Observation to GeoAI: A Systematic Review of Flood Mapping, Susceptibility and Modelling in Malawi
paper_abstract: Flooding is among the most recurrent and damaging hazards in Malawi, yet the geospatial evidence base underpinning flood mapping, susceptibility assessment and modelling remains fragmented. This systematic review synthesises 14 studies published between 2015 and 2026, identified through a PRISMA 2020-compliant search of five databases and supplementary sources, to characterise methodological evolution, spatial coverage, Earth Observation (EO) integration, validation practices and evidence gaps. A bespoke Geospatial Flood Modelling Quality Assessment Framework (GFM-QAF) assessed ten reporting domains (maximum score 20). Findings reveal rapid but recent growth, with 50 % of studies published in 2024 and 2026, alongside a methodological transition from standalone GIS and remote sensing towards integrated EO–GIS–hydrological/hydraulic–machine-learning workflows. Sentinel-1/2 and CHIRPS emerged as the dominant data sources. However, methodological sophistication was not matched by evidential rigour: internal validation predominated, independent spatial/temporal validation remained rare, formal uncertainty propagation was largely absent, and reproducibility was weak (mean GFM-QAF = 12.4/20). Geographically, research clustered in Karonga, Nsanje and the Lower Shire Valley, with national-scale assessments almost absent. Four evidence gaps are identified, geographical, data-related, methodological and evidence-quality, and an evidence-derived Malawi Geospatial Flood-Modelling Framework is proposed, prioritising independent validation, uncertainty quantification, reproducibility and decision-support coupling.

paper_title: Measuring Value in AI Generated Visual Art: A Structured Methodological Review of Valuation Measures
paper_abstract: Studies of AI-generated visual art use value to describe aesthetic ratings, price judgments and acquisition decisions. A synthesis based on these labels alone can combine responses with different meanings. This structured methodological review examines the instruments behind those labels in 12 selected empirical reports from 2018–2026. Targeted searches, reference checking and examination of public methods, supplements and a codebook yielded 25 study units and 46 outcome-family records. Classification distinguished question content, response format and financial consequences, with separate records for source attribution and the object evaluated. Seven study units included economic wording answered without currency; five elicited sale-price judgments, five personal monetary willingness to pay, four purchase intentions or relative buying preferences, and two consequential auction bids. Categories overlap, including within mixed composites. Close reading identified scaled payment questions, a selling-price prediction described as willingness to pay, and an aesthetic-value composite containing economic items. Both auction samples came from one report. The contribution is a classification linked to source passages and a set of reporting fields that preserve these distinctions. For synthesis, a change in rated worth, a recommended or predicted selling price and a consequential bid should be interpreted as different outcomes. For new experiments, the question, response unit and acquisition rule need to be specified together.

paper_title: From ‘Rape’ to Sexual Violence: The Evolution of Definitions, Measurement, Reporting, and Epidemiology of Sexual Assault in the United States, 1900–2026: A Historical-Methodological Review
paper_abstract: For most of the twentieth century, the official United States definition of rape—"the carnal knowledge of a female forcibly and against her will"—rendered most sexual victimization invisible to law, crime statistics, and epidemiology. This review traces the evolution of legal definitions, measurement technologies, reporting behavior, and epidemiological knowledge of sexual assault in the United States from 1900 through 2026, synthesizing legal history, survey methodology, national and campus prevalence studies, and meta-analytic evidence on consequences. Three revolutions define this history. First, statutory reform between the 1970s and 1990s abolished corroboration and resistance requirements, enacted rape shield protections, and made sexual assault laws gender neutral. Second, the federal statistical definition was revised in 2012-2013 to a gender-neutral, consent-based penetration standard, immediately raising officially recorded counts by more than a third. Third, behaviorally specific measurement—pioneered in the late 1970s and validated in 1987—showed that prevalence estimates from such instruments exceed those from crime-survey questions by four- to eleven-fold. Contemporary surveillance places lifetime attempted or completed rape at 18.3% of United States women and 1.4% of men, concentrated in adolescence and young adulthood and overwhelmingly unreported. Reporting research reveals persistent rape myths and negative institutional reactions as filters that suppress counts and compound harm, while intersectional and life-course analyses show exposure and consequence stratified by race, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, and cumulative adversity. The history of sexual assault in the United States is largely the history of its definitions and instruments; unresolved issues of harmonization, inclusivity, and standardization define the methodological agenda ahead.

paper_title: Human Genetic Variants Associated with Susceptibility and Clinical Outcomes in Staphylococcus aureus Infection: A Systematic Review
paper_abstract: Staphylococcus aureus causes diverse clinical manifestations, from asymptomatic colonization to severe invasive disease. Host genetic factors influencing infection susceptibility and severity remain incompletely understood. This systematic review, conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines and registered in PROSPERO, evaluated human genetic variants associated with susceptibility to S.aureus infection and colonization, with subsequent clinical outcomes. Bibliographic databases and grey literature sources were searched for observational studies (2015-2026), with risk of bias assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Regarding innate immunity, IL1RN*2/*2 was associated with post-traumatic S. aureus osteomyelitis, whereas the TIRAP association lost significance after adjustment. In adaptive immunity, admixture mapping linked European ancestry at HLA class II locus to bacteremia in African Americans, while CCR5Δ32 altered circulating chemokines levels without altering clinical risk. Regarding metabolism and iron regulation, GLS2 variant (rs937115) was associated with complicated bacteremia, and an intergenic CHCHD7/SDR16C5 variant (rs73596248) was linked to higher hepcidin levels and a lower risk of bacteremia. CFTR F508del genotype showed no significant association with methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) acquisition. These findings support a multifactorial host genetic network in S. aureus infection and underscore the need for larger, multi-ancestry, independently replicated studies to validate genetic markers for future risk stratification.

paper_title: Stem Cell‐Loaded vs. Extracellular Vesicle‐Loaded Hydrogels: A Comparative Review of Their Potential in Regenerative Medicine
paper_abstract: Hydrogels are being investigated as delivery platforms for stem cells and extracellular vesicles (EVs) in regenerative medicine, but their relative advantages remain unclear. The objective of this critical narrative literature review is to compare stem‐cell‐loaded and EV‐loaded hydrogels in terms of biological activity, cell viability where applicable, retention and controlled release, stability, storage, safety, and clinical development. Published scientiﬁc studies were critically examined, considering experimental conditions, reported outcomes, methodological limitations, and levels of evidence. Stem‐cell‐loaded hydrogels can support living cells and their dynamic interactions with surrounding tissues but require maintenance of cell viability and control of cellular behavior. EV‐loaded hydrogels oﬀer a cell‐free approach that avoids the administration of living therapeutic cells, although vesicle characterization, stability, dosing, and eﬀective delivery remain challenges. Preclinical studies suggest improved local retention and sustained EV release, along with regenerative and immunomodulatory eﬀects in speciﬁc experimental models. However, diﬀerences in hydrogel formulations, experimental conditions, and evaluation methods limit direct comparisons, while clinical eﬀectiveness remains insuﬃciently established. Stimuli‐responsive hydrogels may provide additional control over EV delivery and regulate the microenvironment surrounding encapsulated stem cells, although their therapeutic superiority over conventional systems has not been demonstrated. Overall, neither strategy can currently be considered universally superior. Further research involving standardized characterization, direct comparative studies, long‐term safety evaluations, and clinical validation is necessary to determine their relative therapeutic potential.

paper_title: Various Subtypes of Endometriosis and Cardiovascular Disease: Emerging Molecular Links and Clinical Implications: A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Endometriosis is associated with increased cardiovascular risk, but how its subtype heterogeneity informs this association remains unclear. This narrative review examines the biological characteristics of superficial peritoneal endometriosis (SUP), ovarian endometrioma (OMA), and deep infiltrating endometriosis (DIE) and their potential cardiovascular relevance. English-language literature identified through PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, and reference screening was synthesized across susceptibility factors, molecular and vascular alterations, and treatment exposures. Subtype-related findings highlight differences in anatomical location and tissue microenvironment, including peritoneal immune interactions in superficial lesions, intracystic iron accumulation and oxidative injury in OMA, and inflammatory and fibromuscular remodeling in deep lesions. These features provide a basis for investigating how lesion heterogeneity may relate to systemic lipid dysregulation, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and coagulation abnormalities. Ovarian function, surgical history, and hormonal regimens further inform interpretation of these relationships. By integrating phenotype and treatment exposure while distinguishing local findings from circulating biomarkers, vascular measurements, and clinical events, this review identifies evidence gaps linking biological heterogeneity to cardiovascular outcomes. Emerging subtype-related evidence supports further investigation but does not establish differences in cardiovascular event risk among SUP, OMA, and DIE. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether incorporating endometriosis subtype improves cardiovascular risk assessment beyond conventional factors. (Figure 1)

paper_title: Geometric Algebra for Neural Networks: A Survey
paper_abstract: Geometric algebra (GA) unifies geometric primitives and transformations in a single algebraic framework. Neural networks designed around this framework often represent features as multivectors and constrain layer operations to respect the algebraic structure, enabling principled treatment of geometric transformations and, in many cases, built-in equivariance. This survey reviews geometric algebra neural networks, including their building blocks, equivariant properties, application domains, empirical performance, and software support. We provide an algebra-selection guide, an empirical comparison of GA-based and other equivariant architectures, and a failure-mode analysis covering training pathologies, deployment constraints, and performance limitations. Across the surveyed literature, the strongest evidence for GA-based architectures appears in settings with explicit geometric symmetries and heterogeneous geometric entities; evidence for broader advantages in parameter efficiency, interpretability, and dense prediction is comparatively limited and uneven. We therefore conclude that geometric algebra neural networks are not universally superior to well-tuned non-GA equivariant baselines, and outline open problems in algebra selection, numerical stability, scalable implementation, and reproducible evaluation.

paper_title: The Path to NDE 4.0: A Review of Algorithms, Techniques, and Strategies for Autonomous Inspection
paper_abstract: Non-Destructive Inspection (NDI) is a cornerstone of modern quality assurance, critical for ensuring the safety and reliability of infrastructure and manufactured components without causing damage. This paper presents a comprehensive review of the current NDI landscape, analyzing the field through four distinct lenses, namely, computational algorithms, physical techniques, industrial applications, and research objectives. We synthesize a broad range of academic literature to illustrate the rapid evolution from manual, analog interpretation to a digitized, data-centric paradigm known as NDE 4.0. Our analysis highlights the dominance of ultrasound and visual inspection as primary physical techniques, while revealing a significant shift toward deep learning and generative models for automated defect recognition. Despite these technological strides, the industry faces critical bottlenecks, notably the scarcity of standardized open-access datasets and the "black box" nature of AI models, which hinders widespread adoption. By charting these developments and identifying key research gaps, such as the need for explainable AI (XAI) and standardized digital twin protocols, this review offers a strategic roadmap for future research. It concludes that the future of NDI research should focus on the successful integration of intelligent, autonomous fusion of inspection data with advanced sensor technologies into asset lifecycle management.

paper_title: Knowing When to Hand Over: A Survey of Uncertainty, Deferral, and Escalation in Human–AI Fraud Investigation
paper_abstract: Language-model agents are being proposed to investigate fraud and money-laundering alerts under selective autonomy: the agent closes some cases itself and escalates the rest to a human analyst. Which cases it escalates determines the division of labor, the analysts' workload, and the errors that reach customers and regulators, yet the knowledge needed to design that rule is divided among learning to defer and selective prediction, uncertainty estimation for language models, and research on human reliance on AI advice. This survey connects the three through the escalation loop of a fraud-investigation team and restates known results from these literatures in one notation. We state the cost-optimal escalation rule, which requires different confidence thresholds for closing a case as benign and for concluding fraud, and its form under a fixed analyst capacity; show that calibration suffices for selective risk to be monotone and interpretable; state the conformal bound on the rate of cases that are both closed automatically and wrong; show when combining uncertainty signals helps and when correlated signals double-count; show that the error among automatically closed cases is not identified without audits and is estimable with them; and quantify how analyst reliance on the agent's verdict erodes the value of escalation. Against this basis we compare deferral rules and uncertainty signals, and conclude that threshold-based deferral rules assume a calibrated confidence that agents do not yet provide, that agent-level uncertainty estimation is only beginning, and that, to our knowledge, no peer-reviewed study has yet evaluated an escalation rule for a fraud-investigation agent together with the analysts who receive its cases.

paper_title: Review of the Association Between Neck Circumference and Multisystem Diseases: From an Anthropometric Indicator to a Clinical Risk Marker
paper_abstract: Background: Obesity is a core risk factor for multiple chronic diseases. Adipose tissue distribution has greater predictive value for metabolic and cardiovascular risk than total fat mass. Neck circumference, a simple anthropometric indicator of upper-body subcutaneous fat accumulation, has gained increasing attention in recent years for its value in metabolic and cardiovascular risk stratification.Objective: To systematically search for and synthesize evidence on the association between neck circumference and multisystem diseases and to evaluate the evidence base and key challenges for translating neck circumference from an anthropometric indicator into a clinical risk marker.Methods: This review is a systematically searched narrative review. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and CNKI were searched from database inception to June 30, 2026. A supplementary search was performed for 2026 articles published online after the search cutoff date. Systematic reviews and meta-analyses of the association between neck circumference and disease or risk factors served as the primary evidence source and were supplemented by large prospective cohort studies and key cross-sectional studies. Case reports, small-sample uncontrolled studies, purely hypothetical articles, conference abstracts, preprints, and registered trial protocols were excluded. Evidence was synthesized narratively, and effect sizes were not pooled. The review was not prospectively registered, and no formal evidence grading was performed with tools such as GRADE. Related limitations are discussed in Section 9.1.Results: A total of 130 articles were included. Current evidence indicates that increased neck circumference is epidemiologically associated with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), components of metabolic syndrome (MetS), dyslipidemia, obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), atrial fibrillation, heart failure, ischemic stroke, chronic kidney disease (CKD), hyperuricemia, gout, and the risk of cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality. Associations with left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH), cardiac electrical remodeling, subclinical atherosclerosis, arterial stiffness, retinal microvascular changes, decline in lung function, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), coronary heart disease, cognitive impairment, and reduced brain gray matter volume have also been reported, but the evidence is weaker, inconsistent in direction, or confined to subgroups. The prognosis of hemorrhagic stroke also requires further validation. The direction of associations for geriatric and nutritional outcomes such as sarcopenia, malnutrition, and decline in activities of daily living (ADL) is inconsistent, with some studies showing risk associated with lower neck circumference; presarcopenic obesity, in contrast, is positively associated with increased neck circumference. Evidence for associations with metabolic syndrome in children with type 1 diabetes mellitus, bone mineral density, depression, and sleep quality is weak, inconsistent in direction, or confined to specific subgroups. Some associations, such as those for T2DM and hypertension, remain significant after adjustment for body mass index (BMI), and the CKD evidence is partially supportive. Evidence strength was judged comprehensively based on study design, cross-population consistency, whether associations remained significant after adjustment for BMI or waist circumference, and the availability of Mendelian randomization (MR) evidence; overall, the evidence was heterogeneous. However, neck circumference is strongly collinear with waist circumference and BMI. Some meta-analyses have shown no significant association between neck circumference and the composite MetS endpoint. The Jackson Heart Study found no independent association between neck circumference and cardiovascular outcomes after full adjustment. MR studies have shown a protective causal association between neck circumference and metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD), contradicting observational studies; other MR studies have not found a causal association between neck circumference and bone mineral density. Wrist circumference outperforms neck circumference in predicting insulin resistance in children, and in children with type 1 diabetes mellitus, waist circumference has a higher area under the curve (AUC) than neck circumference for predicting MetS. Causality has not yet been fully established. Genetic evidence indicates that neck circumference has a genetic basis independent of overall obesity. Intervention studies suggest that neck circumference can be changed by lifestyle interventions, but its changes are not fully synchronized with improvements in neck adipose tissue or core OSA endpoints. Evidence from nontraditional cardiovascular risk markers, mechanistic studies, studies in special populations, measurement standardization studies, and evidence on local effects in head and neck cancer has further expanded the boundaries of clinical application of neck circumference. Prospective evidence in the field of nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) shows that in postmenopausal women with normal BMI, baseline neck circumference still independently predicts NAFLD incidence. Studies in young Chinese adults suggest that there are significant sex differences in the performance of neck circumference for diagnosing obesity.Conclusions: As a systematically searched narrative review, this review suggests that neck circumference is epidemiologically associated with multisystem diseases, but the strength of evidence is heterogeneous. Current evidence supports its use as an adjunctive indicator for risk screening; however, it cannot yet serve as an independent causal risk marker. Cross-disease comparisons of effect sizes are influenced by differences in indicator type, baseline risk, and follow-up duration and should not be used as a direct basis for clinical decision-making.

paper_title: Challenges and Opportunities for Kaposi Sarcoma Clinical Trials in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Review
paper_abstract: Kaposi sarcoma is a vascular tumor that remains a significant global public health challenge, with approximately 70% of cases occurring in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), where Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) and Human Herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) are highly prevalent. Furthermore, relatively few clinical trials have been conducted in SSA, potentially delaying the development of more effective interventions for this cancer. This review evaluated completed prospective clinical trials for the treatment of HIV-associated Kaposi sarcoma (KS) conducted in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) and highlighted the complementary role of investigator-initiated clinical trials in drug development. We searched the internet and medical databases using relevant key terms. We identified 171 indexed HIV-KS clinical trials worldwide and extracted seven that were conducted in SSA between 1984 and July 2022. The first trial took place in Zimbabwe and was published in 2005. The second and third trials were conducted in South Africa and published in 2008 and 2012, respectively. The fourth and sixth trials were done in Kenya, Uganda, South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Brazil, and were published in 2018 and 2020. The fifth was an investigator-initiated trial (IIT) done in Kenya and published in 2018 and 2019. The sixth trial featured the largest sample size and the most diverse study population. The seventh evaluated the effectiveness of locally sourced compression bandages for HIV-KS leg lymphedema in Kenya and was published in 2022. The number of clinical trials for interventions to treat HIV-KS in SSA remains disproportionate to the high burden of disease in the region. Highlighting research gaps may stimulate interest in studies aimed at finding a cure for HIV-KS in sub-Saharan Africa.

paper_title: Photovoltaic Inverters as Grid-Balancing Actuators: A Constraint-Stack Review of Controllability, Interoperability, and Aggregation
paper_abstract: Photovoltaic inverters are the devices that actually change solar output on the distribution network, yet reviews of virtual power plants often treat them as abstract units that can simply be dispatched. This review therefore starts from the device. A solar system is controllable only when three things are true together: the inverter can change its behaviour, there is a way to send that change, and someone is allowed to send it. On the way up from the device, grid codes, communication choices, the path used to reach the inverter, and market rules each remove part of what the nameplate suggests. Four results follow from this view. First, inverters with the same rated power do not behave in the same way, and reactive-power support shortens inverter life. Second, standards agree on what a function means but not on how it is written in the message, so the cost of adding devices grows with the number of manufacturers. Third, choosing between a manufacturer cloud and a local controller is mainly a choice about who can still give orders when the link fails. Fourth, changing output when the network needs it keeps much more solar energy than a fixed capacity limit, but it does not replace network upgrades, the loss is not shared evenly, and a saved kilowatt-hour is not the same thing as avoided emissions. Overall, the tightest limits are interoperability, different national rules, reactive power that is required but not paid, and cybersecurity duties that are weaker than the control duties.

paper_title: A Systematic Survey on Unified Compression-Encryption Schemes with a Header-Consolidation Taxonomy
paper_abstract: Data compression and encryption are conventionally performed as sequential operations, incurring redundant computational overhead, increasing the attack surface, and complicating system architectures. This systematic literature review analyzes 34 verified contributions published between 1948 and 2026 in IEEE, ACM, Springer, Elsevier, Wiley, IET, and NIST venues, following PRISMA 2020. We propose a four-level operational taxonomy (L0–L3) for defining what it means for a scheme to be unified rather than merely coordinated as well as the structure of header consolidation: an L3 scheme consolidates the compression and encryption headers into a single object, typically carried by the key. Only two schemes achieve L3, both restricted by domain-specific assumptions. We discover two structural constraints—the redundancy duality and the header duality—which explain why L3 schemes are restricted to domain-specific, and that the latter is a security constraint: the compression header leaks source statistics and the encryption header leaks cryptographic state, so consolidating them reduces the attack surface. We also show that source-type specificity is inherited by all joint schemes reviewed, and the review also reveals that no scheme achieves a source-independent compression ratio, and that formal security proofs under standard adversarial models (IND-CPA, IND-CCA, IND-CCA2, AE) are absent in each of the reviewed schemes, including the two L3 schemes.

paper_title: Navigating the Control Landscape: A Mathematical Survey and Operational Decision Matrix for 34 Control Methodologies
paper_abstract: Control engineering has undergone a transformative evolution, progressing from rudimentary relay-based regulators to highly sophisticated adaptive, robust, and data-driven intelligent architectures. This paper provides an intensive and structured survey of thirty-four distinct control techniques, categorized into classical compensators (P, PI, PD, PID, Lead-Lag), structural extensions (Feedforward, Cascade, Smith Predictor, IMC), modern state-space methods (LQR, LQG, Kalman Filter, MPC), robust designs ($H_\infty$, $\mu$-Synthesis, QFT), adaptive strategies (MRAC, Self-Tuning, Gain Scheduling), nonlinear approaches (Sliding Mode, Backstepping, Feedback Linearization, Lyapunov), and intelligent soft-computing systems (Fuzzy, Neural Networks, Reinforcement Learning, ANFIS). A defining feature of this review is the rigorous mapping of every control methodology to its original foundational reference, providing a comprehensive historical and theoretical lineage for each system. For each category, we derive the fundamental mathematical models governing controller behavior. The paper concludes with a comprehensive classification table and an operational decision matrix, evaluating techniques based on implementation domain, practical difficulty, and model-dependency to serve as an evidence-based, expert-informed decision framework for selecting appropriate control paradigms based on plant complexities and environmental constraints.

paper_title: Admission Inflammatory Biomarkers and New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation After Acute Myocardial Infarction: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
paper_abstract: Background: New-onset atrial fibrillation (NOAF) complicates acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and worsens prognosis. Systemic inflammation may contribute, but the value of admission inflammatory biomarkers is uncertain.Methods: Following PRISMA 2020 (PROSPERO CRD420261470060), we searched six databases from inception to 26 September 2026 for observational studies comparing admission neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), C-reactive protein (CRP), or high-sensitivity CRP (hs-CRP) between AMI patients with and without NOAF. Risk of bias was assessed with QUIPS and certainty of evidence with GRADE. We used random-effects models, prediction intervals, leave-one-out sensitivity analyses, and Doi plots with the LFK index.Results: Sixteen studies (12,509 patients; 1,103 with NOAF) were included. NOAF was associated with higher NLR (MD 1.78, 95% CI 0.44 to 3.11; I² 70.6%), CRP (MD 4.17, 1.42 to 6.91; I² 53.8%), and hs-CRP (SMD 0.84, 0.47 to 1.20; I² 88.6%). PLR did not differ significantly (three studies; MD 57.19, 95% CI −13.38 to 127.77). CRP and hs-CRP remained significant in every leave-one-out analysis, whereas NLR lost significance after omitting one study (p = 0.055). All prediction intervals crossed no effect. Funnel plots, Doi plots, and LFK indices (2.46 to 7.25) indicated asymmetry. Certainty of evidence was very low for all biomarkers.Conclusion: Higher admission NLR, CRP, and hs-CRP are associated with NOAF after AMI, but the evidence is very low certainty and PLR findings are inconclusive. These markers cannot yet identify individual high-risk patients; prospective studies with standardized sampling, continuous rhythm monitoring, and adjusted analyses are needed.

paper_title: Bruxism in Older Adults Aged 60 Years and Over: Assessment, Epidemiology, Associated Factors, and Management – A Scoping Review
paper_abstract: Bruxism is a repetitive masticatory muscle activity occurring during sleep or wakefulness, yet evidence specific to older adults remains dispersed across disciplines. This scoping review mapped the evidence on bruxism in adults aged ≥60 years regarding conceptualisation, assessment, epidemiology, associated factors, and management. Following PRISMA-ScR guidance, PubMed, CINAHL, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched for primary studies involving adults aged ≥60 years or reporting separable data for this age group. Two reviewers screened records independently. Of 1227 records identified, 1045 were screened, 80 full texts were assessed, and 34 studies were included. Most were observational studies (64.7%) or case-based reports (32.4%), and most used an unspecified bruxism construct (64.7%). Assessment was predominantly non-instrumental; only six studies used polysomnography or electromyography. Reported associated factors included temporomandibular disorders, orofacial pain, sleep disorders, neurodegenerative disease, stroke, medication exposure, tooth wear, and prosthetic complications. Management evidence was scarce and largely case-based. Evidence on bruxism in later life is fragmented and methodologically heterogeneous. Future studies should report older-adult data separately, distinguish sleep from awake bruxism, and apply standardised assessment frameworks.

paper_title: Fungal Infections in People Living with HIV and Other Immunocompromised Patients: A European and Romanian Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Background. Fungal infections are a major cause of morbidity and mortality across the growing population of immunocompromised patients, although the underlying immune deficit differs between people living with HIV/AIDS, non-HIV hosts (hematologic malignancy, neutropenia, solid organ or hematopoietic stem cell transplantation), and critically ill patients rendered transiently immunosuppressed by severe illness itself, as during the COVID-19 pandemic. Objectives. To compare epidemiology, pathogens, diagnosis, treatment, resistance, and prophylaxis across HIV, non-HIV immunocompromised hosts, and COVID-19-associated fungal disease, and to examine, as a regional case study, how this picture is represented in the European literature and in Romania specifically. Methods. Narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE literature on HIV and non-HIV immunocompromising conditions, including COVID-19 associated conditions, complemented by a targeted search for European cohort data and by pathogen-specific PubMed searches for Romanian primary literature. Diagnostic terminology follows the EORTC/MSGERC consensus definitions, complemented by the ECMM/ISHAM criteria for COVID-19-associated pulmonary aspergillosis (CAPA). Results. CD4+ depletion in HIV produces a predictable, threshold-driven pattern of opportunistic mycoses; non-HIV immunosuppression is more heterogeneous; and critical illness — as exemplified by COVID-19 — introduced a distinct risk state, with COVID-19 Associated Pulmonary Aspergillosis (CAPA) incidence ranging from ~1% to >20% in ICU patients across European cohorts, and COVID-19-associated mucormycosis (CAM) reaching epidemic proportions in India. European cohorts otherwise document a one-year invasive fungal disease incidence of ~10% after allogeneic HSCT, up to 17% in acute leukemia, and 3–14% for aspergillosis after lung transplantation. Romanian evidence consists of single-center mycological studies, three Candidozyma (Candida) auris reports (including a genomic study assigning all sequenced isolates to clade I), case reports and small series of aspergillosis, CAPA and mucormycosis (the latter increasing after COVID-19), a nosocomial fusariosis outbreak in an acute leukemia ward, one cryptococcal-meningitis series, environmental detection of azole-resistant Aspergillus fumigatus, and a modelled national burden estimate; no dedicated series exist in solid organ transplant recipients or patients with solid tumors. Conclusions. Recognizing these divergent, population- and context-specific patterns is essential to risk-stratified screening and treatment; the Romanian case illustrates how national surveillance can lag far behind recognized burden even within a well-characterized global framework.

paper_title: Analgesia During Prolonged Wilderness Evacuation: A Focused Systematic Review and Targeted Meta-Analysis of Practical Prehospital Strategies
paper_abstract: Background: Pain management in wilderness and austere care must balance humane, effective analgesia against limited monitoring, environmental exposure, restricted drug inventories, and evacuation delays that may last hours. This review evaluates practical analgesic strategies for prolonged wilderness evacuation and quantitatively synthesizes directly comparable prehospital ketamine-versus-morphine trials. Methods: A focused systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE-indexed literature and backward citation chaining was conducted through September 5, 2026. Human prehospital, wilderness, remote, austere, and prolonged-field-care studies evaluating acetaminophen, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), opioids, ketamine, or regional anesthesia were prioritized. Guidelines and systematic reviews were used to contextualize operational feasibility. A random-effects meta-analysis pooled studies reporting directly comparable changes in 0-10 pain intensity for ketamine versus morphine. Results: Direct evidence specific to prolonged civilian wilderness evacuation was sparse. Across the broader prehospital literature, acetaminophen and NSAIDs provided useful low-complexity analgesia for mild-to-moderate pain and as components of multimodal therapy. Opioids remained effective for severe pain but impose respiratory, hemodynamic, nausea, sedation, and monitoring burdens. Ketamine produced analgesia broadly comparable with morphine in contemporary randomized trials, with faster onset in some studies and a different adverse-effect profile characterized by more emergence phenomena but less opioid-associated nausea, hypotension, or respiratory compromise in some datasets. Two directly comparable trials (n=559) yielded a pooled mean difference in pain-score change of -0.27 points favoring ketamine (95% CI, -0.70 to 0.17; I2=13%), indicating no clinically important difference in analgesic efficacy. Regional techniques, particularly fascia iliaca compartment block for proximal femur injury, showed substantial opioid-sparing potential when performed by trained clinicians. Conclusions: No single agent is optimal for prolonged wilderness evacuation. The most defensible strategy is staged multimodal analgesia matched to pain severity, physiology, evacuation duration, provider skill, and monitoring capacity. Oral acetaminophen and/or an NSAID form a practical foundation when not contraindicated; severe pain may justify titrated ketamine or an opioid, while regional anesthesia can be valuable for selected injuries. The major evidence gap is not short-term analgesic efficacy but safety, redosing, monitoring, and functional outcomes during evacuations lasting many hours.

paper_title: Maternal Omega-3 Fatty Acid Exposure During Pregnancy and Childhood Allergic Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Exploratory Meta-Analysis
paper_abstract: Background: Prenatal exposure to omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (n-3 PUFAs) may influence immune development, but associations with allergic disorders in childhood remain inconsistent. Objective: To evaluate the association of maternal omega-3 exposure during pregnancy with childhood asthma, wheeze, eczema, and allergic nasal disease. Methods: This systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis included 13 independent study populations contributing 22 outcome-specific estimates. Prenatal dietary intake, biomarkers, fish consumption, and supplementation were considered. Random-effects models used restricted maximum likelihood (REML) estimation with modified Knapp-Hartung inference; pooled effects are presented as log odds ratios (logORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).Results: For asthma (k = 5), pooled logOR was -0.240 (95% CI -0.444 to -0.036; p = 0.031; I² = 0.0%). For wheeze (k = 5), logOR was -0.071 (95% CI -0.176 to 0.035; p = 0.137; I² = 31.3%). For eczema (k = 7), logOR was -0.106 (95% CI -0.839 to 0.627; p = 0.736; I² = 78.4%). For allergic nasal disease (k = 5), logOR was -0.078 (95% CI -0.461 to 0.305; p = 0.602; I² = 72.8%). Conclusions: Higher maternal omega-3 exposure was associated with lower pooled odds of childhood asthma, whereas associations for the other outcomes were statistically inconclusive. Differences in exposure definitions, study designs, and allergy phenotypes limit causal interpretation.
paper_authors: Maria Adriely Machado de Castro Oliveira

paper_title: From Scorecards to Agents: A Survey of Anti-Fraud Models Across the Model-Risk Boundary, with a Focus on Evidence Traceability
paper_abstract: The revised United States guidance on model risk management, issued in April 2026, applies its principles to traditional statistical and quantitative models and to non-generative, non-agentic AI models, and places generative and agentic AI explicitly outside its scope. This survey follows the models used against fraud and financial crime across that line, from rules, scorecards, and statistical tests, through non-generative machine learning, to generative models and language-model agents, across six fraud types. Unlike prior surveys, we place all three generations in one decision-theoretic frame: we restate in one notation known results on cost-optimal and capacity-constrained alerting, undersampling calibration, and the identifiability of recall from alert feedback, express each generation's model, explanation, and validation quantity in that frame, and add two stylized models, one showing why mean aggregation dilutes the neighborhood signal of camouflaged fraudsters and one showing how verifier independence bounds the residual errors in a generated narrative. We find that statistical models and non-generative machine learning have mature validation practice anchored in supervisory guidance, that generative AI now appears both as a tool of fraudsters and as a component of defenses, and that in hybrid pipelines the generative component can write what an analyst or examiner reads although no dedicated supervisory framework covers it. We therefore formalize the evidence-traceability controls that can supply this missing validation as a division of verification labor, between the drafting agent, a deterministic field check, an independent verifier and the human examiner, governed by three parameters an institution can estimate; we then compare the generations quantity by quantity and close with a research agenda.

paper_title: Optimizing the Chain of Survival: European OHCA Outcomes and Reporting Standards—A Scoping Review
paper_abstract: Background: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remains a major public health challenge across Europe. While prehospital emergency medical services (EMS) vary widely, the degree to which regional infrastructure, dispatch guidance, and community responder frameworks influence clinical outcomes when mapped against standardized reporting templates remains insufficiently synthe-sized. This scoping review evaluates European OHCA evidence across standardized Utstein re-porting domains to analyze prehospital system factors, responder interventions, and clinical out-comes. Methods: Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines and Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology, a systematic literature search was performed across PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science (January 2021–March 2026). From 8,882 records identified, 2,126 full-text articles were evaluated using a Population, Exposure, Outcome (PEO) framework. Data were synthesized across four core Utstein domains. Results: Forty three primary studies (N = 43) were included. System Factors demonstrated that prolonged ambulance response intervals severely diminish survival, particularly in sparsely populated rural sectors. Dispatch Protocols highlighted that rapid dispatcher recognition signifi-cantly increases telephone CPR instructions and community resource activation. Under bystander a prominent gap was identified between public AED availability and actual lay bystander deployment (< 5%). Dispatched Volunteer Community Responders (VCR) and First Responders (FR) achieved median arrival time-gains of 4–5 minutes; however, survival benefits were descriptively observed primarily when early arrival facilitated ultra-early defibrillation or high-quality CPR. Clinical Out-comes confirmed that 30-day survival and favorable neurological recovery (CPC 1–2) remain highly variable, heavily constrained by reporting heterogeneity. Conclusions: Strengthening early links in the chain of survival—specifically dispatcher recognition, app-alerted volunteer dispatch, and public defibrillation—is consistently associated with improved clinical survival. Universal adoption of the updated Utstein 2024 reporting template is essential to eliminate reporting heterogeneity and enable meaningful cross-system benchmarks across Europe.

paper_title: Vaginal Dysbiosis in Women’s Reproductive Health: A Critical Review of Clinical Associations, Diagnostic Challenges, and Therapeutic Perspectives
paper_abstract: The vaginal microbiota represents a dynamic microbial ecosystem that contributes to mucosal homeostasis and protection against potentially pathogenic microorganisms. Vaginal dysbiosis, characterized by alterations in microbial composition and function, has increasingly been associated with gynecological, reproductive, obstetric, and puerperal conditions. This review summarizes current evidence on the composition and determinants of the vaginal microbiota, with an emphasis on Community State Types and major forms of dysbiosis, including bacterial vaginosis, vulvovaginal candidiasis, aerobic vaginitis, and viral infections. The associations between dysbiosis and sexually transmitted infections are discussed, with particular attention to the distinction between colonization, dysbiosis, and clinically relevant infection. Potential relationships between dysbiosis and infertility are examined, including tubal, cervical, and endometrial factors, as well as outcomes following assisted reproductive technologies. Evidence regarding obstetric and puerperal complications is critically evaluated. Finally, current therapeutic strategies are reviewed, ranging from etiological antimicrobial treatment to probiotics, defined live biotherapeutics, and emerging approaches such as vaginal microbiota transplantation. Although microbiota restoration represents a promising therapeutic concept, uncertainties remain regarding optimal strains, timing, diagnostic criteria, and clinically meaningful outcomes. Overall, vaginal dysbiosis should be regarded not simply as a local microbial imbalance but as a condition capable of modifying mucosal host-pathogen interactions throughout the female reproductive tract.

paper_title: AI in Education from CAI to AGI: A Narrative Review and Conceptual Framework
paper_abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping education, yet research remains fragmented across technological streams and often conflates technical capability with demonstrated educational effectiveness. This narrative review synthesizes representative literature published mainly between 2010 and 2026 to trace the evolution of AI-enabled education from computer-assisted instruction toward adaptive, immersive, generative, and potentially more general forms of intelligence. It compares three major technological streams: intelligent tutoring and adaptive learning systems, extended reality (XR), and large language model-based generative AI. The review finds that intelligent tutoring systems support learner modeling, adaptive feedback, and personalization, but their evidence base is methodologically heterogeneous. XR shows comparatively more consolidated evidence, particularly through systematic reviews and meta-analyses, with generally positive but context-dependent effects on engagement and learning outcomes. Generative AI expands dialogic explanation, scaffolding, content generation, and personalized support, although learner-outcome evidence remains limited relative to capability benchmarking. Building on these findings, the review proposes a Technology–Mechanism–Outcome–Challenge framework and argues that future progress toward artificial general intelligence (AGI) should be evaluated through learning mechanisms, measurable outcomes, human oversight, equity, and responsible governance.

paper_title: Chart Reasoning with Multimodal Large Language Models: A Survey
paper_abstract: Chart reasoning requires multimodal models to interpret visual encodings, derive structured semantics, execute formal reasoning procedures, and generate evidence-grounded outputs. This survey reviews chart reasoning methodologies for multimodal large language models (MLLMs), categorizing them by their primary intervention points: data and supervision design, inference-time reasoning strategies, and model-integrated optimization. We examine how existing approaches extract chart semantics, use intermediate representations, execute reasoning workflows, ground predictions in visual evidence, and verify outputs. We also summarize major chart reasoning benchmarks and cross-paradigm empirical results, and examine limitations in current evaluation protocols and metrics. Finally, we discuss recurring challenges in synthetic-to-real generalization, semantic reconstruction, visual grounding, reasoning faithfulness, and diagnostic evaluation, outlining directions toward more reliable and generalizable chart reasoning systems.

paper_title: Mapping the Research Landscape of Teacher Digital Competence: A Bibliometric and Literature Review
paper_abstract: Objective: Teachers’ digital competence is increasingly important for meeting contemporary curricular demands and integrating educational technology effectively into formal learning environments. Beyond basic technical proficiency, this multidimensional construct encompasses the cognitive, motor, social, and emotional skills needed for effective teaching. Methodology: This study combined bibliometric mapping with a systematic literature review (SLR), following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, to examine the structural and thematic landscape of research on teachers’ digital competence. The analysis included 63 peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2020 and December 2025 and retrieved from Scopus. Bibliometric mapping and thematic synthesis were used to examine research trends and thematic clusters. Results: The findings suggest a shift from policy-oriented formulations toward the practical integration of competence frameworks across educational contexts. Four prominent areas of research were competence assessment, analysis of correlates, validation of measurement instruments, and professional development and training. Established frameworks, particularly DigCompEdu, TPACK, and the Common Framework for Teachers’ Digital Competence (MCCDD), guided the implementation of digital competence through interactive media, personalized learning, data-driven decision-making, and digital citizenship education. Conclusions: The reviewed literature suggests a shift from the operational mastery of technical tools toward the strategic, standardized, and pedagogically grounded integration of educational technology into teaching.

paper_title: Methodological Determinants of Fungal Identification by Proteomic Mass Spectrometry: A Narrative Review with Emphasis on MALDI-TOF MS
paper_abstract: Matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS) has become the dominant proteomic platform for fungal identification, turning a multi-day, morphology-dependent workflow into a minutes-long protein-fingerprinting assay. Yet reported performance for the same genera ranges from under 20% to over 95% depending on the study. This narrative review examines sources of heterogeneity across five domains: (1) biological and pre-analytical properties, including colony age, growth phase and dimorphism, culture medium, incubation temperature, pigmentation, and taxonomic complexity; (2) sample-processing variables, including protein-extraction chemistry, deposition technique, and matrix selection; (3) instrument-acquisition parameters, including laser intensity, shot number, signal-intensity thresholds, calibration, and cross-platform differences; (4) database and bioinformatic factors, including reference-library completeness, score-threshold interpretation, and software version; and (5) specimen type and clinical context, particularly for culture-independent workflows. The review examines how these factors affect proteomic identification of molds. First, variability attributed to fungal biology may be confounded by methodological variability: studies using standardized, validated extraction protocols may report less variability attributable to biology than studies using less-controlled methods. Second, reference-library completeness and standardized, locally validated sample preparation and deposition are particularly actionable determinants. Third, an unresolved challenge is reliable identification of rare, cryptic, melanized, dimorphic, and emerging organisms. The review concludes with evidence-informed quality-assurance practices considered in the context of CLSI M58.

paper_title: <span data-teams="true">Availability and Access to Cardiovascular Medicines in Mozambique: A Scoping Review
paper_abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are a leading cause of mortality worldwide, with more than 80% of deaths occurring in low- and middle-income countries. In Mozambique, non-communicable diseases account for approximately 28% of deaths, with CVDs contributing substantially to this burden. Despite the country’s hierarchical health system and the World Health Organization target of 80% availability of essential medicines, access to cardiovascular medicines remains poorly documented. This scoping review mapped the availability, prices, affordability, physical access, and health-system barriers affecting access to essential cardiovascular medicines in Mozambique. The review followed the PRISMA-ScR guidelines and the Arksey and O’Malley framework. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were systematically searched without publication-year restrictions. Eligible studies assessed the availability, stock-outs, prices, affordability, or health-system barriers related to cardiovascular medicines and diagnostics in Mozambique. Study selection and data extraction were independently performed by multiple reviewers. Consistent with the scoping review design, formal risk-of-bias assessment was not undertaken. Fifteen studies met the inclusion criteria. Essential cardiovascular medicines showed persistently low availability, with mean availability of approximately 21% across public hospital pharmacies, private retail outlets, and private hospitals, substantially below the WHO 80% target. Public facilities consistently provided only a limited range of older first-line medicines, while second- and third-line medicines, statins, digoxin, direct oral anticoagulants, and diagnostic reagents were frequently unavailable. When public stocks were depleted, patients relied on private-sector purchases, where generic medicines cost an average of 4.51 times international reference prices. Long-term secondary prevention could require 14.0–17.8 days of wages per month for low-income workers. These barriers were associated with low hypertension awareness, treatment, and control, substantial target-organ damage, high stroke case-fatality, and poor anticoagulation control. Access to cardiovascular medicines in Mozambique is severely constrained by low availability, frequent stock-outs, and unaffordable private-sector prices. Strengthening medicine selection, supply-chain management, financial protection, and decentralized protocol-based care is essential to improve equitable access to cardiovascular treatment.

paper_title: Region-Guided Food-Package Evidence Extraction and Abstention-Aware Draft R3337 Screening with Selective VLM Review
paper_abstract: Applying South Africa's draft R3337 warning criteria to food-package photographs requires nutrition, ingredient and product-form evidence. This study presents a region-guided evidence extraction and abstention-aware screening workflow for draft R3337. A three-class detector localises nutrition information panels, ingredient lists and product-identity regions, after which PaddleOCR and structured extraction recover nutrient values, ingredient evidence and product-form information. Recovered evidence is aggregated and assessed using deterministic draft R3337 rules. When evidence is incomplete, uncertain or conflicting, the workflow abstains through Review or Insufficient evidence rather than forcing an automatic outcome. For qualifying unresolved cases, a selective vision-language model (VLM) review stage using Qwen3-VL 8B Instruct reassesses unresolved evidence. Accepted evidence is merged and the same deterministic rules are reapplied. The workflow was applied to 442 products represented by 3,929 images. Evaluation used a manual validation set of 65 products. Before selective VLM review, 31 of 60 decidable products received automatic outcomes and 30 were correct, giving 51.7% coverage and 96.8% accuracy among automatic outcomes (selective accuracy). Selective VLM review resolved eight additional products, increasing coverage to 65.0%. Of 39 automatic outcomes, 38 were correct, giving 97.4% selective accuracy. The single false warning was retained from the rules-only workflow, while no unsafe warning omissions occurred after selective review. Evidence-level evaluation nevertheless identified incorrect VLM-recovered nutrition, ingredient and product-form evidence. These findings show that selective VLM review can recover unresolved evidence, while deterministic screening and explicit abstention remain necessary for reliable image-based draft R3337 screening.

paper_title: InsightRAG: Aggregating Distributed Scholarly Judgments for Scientific Survey Generation
paper_abstract: The rapid growth of scientific literature makes survey writing increasingly challenging, motivating automatic survey generation. Yet, existing systems must search an open space of papers and an open space of concepts with no trace of how the community itself has navigated them, leading to incomplete scope, weak taxonomies, and unreliable citations. Our core insight is that author-written Related Work sections contain the human judgments needed to address both limitations: authors curate the citations relevant to their contributions and explain how the cited works relate, yielding paths for scope reconstruction and relational evidence for organization. We propose InsightRAG. Its insight-guided retrieval follows author-supported citation relations to reconstruct a verified research scope and structure the resulting relational evidence. It aggregates these judgments under a minimum-conflict objective into a taxonomy that reflects recurring author-written perspectives in the retrieved literature, guides generation, and bounds each section's evidence. Results on ten topics show gains in scope reconstruction, taxonomy quality, citation support, and reference reliability.

paper_title: From RL Papers to Framework Code: Inclusion and Review in Seven Open-Source Training Frameworks
paper_abstract: Practitioners use reinforcement learning methods for language models through training frameworks, so a method that a framework includes is one configuration change away for its users. We measure how often this happens. We trace seven open-source frameworks for RL post-training through their commit histories and link them to 6,939 screened arXiv papers from January 2025 to June 2026. Of 1,598 papers that propose a general RL training method, 37 reached at least one framework. Across five quarterly cohorts of papers, the number included within 180 days stayed between 5 and 7 while the cohorts grew from 72 to 386 papers. Compared with papers from the same quarters, included papers more often trained policies of 30B parameters or more, at 41 against 10 percent, and more often changed a coefficient, clip, mask or weight in the existing loss, at 29 against 9 percent. Both gaps hold without papers from the companies that maintain the frameworks, while code release was equally common in both groups. The frameworks' issues and pull requests show that few methods are turned away in public. More than nine in ten of the general methods no framework included have no thread there that cites or names them, and many proposals that do appear stay open without a reply. Two further records, the frameworks' issues and the technical reports of 13 large open-weight models, show that users rarely report training failures in public and that the reports state 8 of the 13 widely included methods. We release the data as a tracker that links training failures to framework implementations and lists each framework's contribution rules and earlier proposals.
comments: 29 pages (13 pages main text), 5 figures, 12 tables. Data and code at https://github.com/pth2002/rl-method-tracker and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23495743

paper_title: The More the Better? A Comparison of Single- and Multi-Agent LLM Setups on a Financial Review Task
paper_abstract: Practitioner guidance holds that a large language model reviews a document better when the work is divided among agents. We test a narrow form of it in a controlled comparison of single-agent and multi-agent setups on a financial task, reviewing credit assessment memos against requirements. One agent checks six requirements in one call. A team of three on the same model checks the same memo, two requirements each, in the same words, with no roles or later stage. Labels are known for every requirement on 300 synthetic memos, so misses and false alarms are measured separately. Two primary predictions are tested on four models at a Bonferroni-corrected level. Under an instruction to decide each requirement once, the team catches 0.08 to 0.10 more of the defects that carry an explanation on the three models whose single agent misses some, at the corrected level on two. It raises more false alarms on all four, at the corrected level on three. Balanced accuracy, an exploratory measure, changes by 0.02 or less, and the team uses 2.2 to 2.4 times the tokens. Showing each agent the requirements it was not given reduces the added false alarms on the two Claude models, at the corrected level on one. In exploratory comparisons, sampling the single agent three times and flagging on any draw gives higher balanced accuracy than the team on those models, and the team's results depend on the instruction.

paper_title: Reinforcement learning for hardware acceleration and system-level optimization on FPGA and integrated-circuit platforms: A survey
paper_abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) enables adaptive and autonomous decision-making in embedded, edge, and heterogeneous computing systems. Field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) and integrated circuits (ICs) offer low latency, energy efficiency, and architectural flexibility for RL deployment, while introducing challenges in resource constraints, implementation complexity, and hardware-algorithm co-design. This review surveys more than 100 studies on RL implementations across FPGA and IC platforms, emphasizing architectures, implementation strategies, performance evaluation, and applications. The literature is organized by RL family, including model-based Markov decision processes, classical value-based methods, deep RL, actor-critic, policy-gradient, and multi-agent approaches. We further classify studies by abstraction level, hardware realization strategy, and application domain, examining how RL algorithms map onto reconfigurable and fixed hardware. Unlike surveys restricted to particular algorithms or platforms, this work provides a unified analysis of FPGA and IC implementations, covering acceleration, reconfigurable architectures, energy-aware control, and system-level optimization. Comparative assessments consider resource utilization, latency, throughput, power consumption, and reported performance gains. Finally, we identify recurring architectural patterns, practical limitations, open challenges, and research directions for efficient RL-driven hardware systems. The survey offers a consolidated reference for researchers developing and evaluating RL solutions on specialized hardware.

paper_title: BCI & AI for Cognitively-Aware Learning: A Review of Technologies, Tools, and Applications
paper_abstract: This article presents a comprehensive review of technologies, tools, and applications in the field of brain-computer interfaces (BCI) and artificial intelligence (AI) for developing cognitively adaptive learning environments. Unlike prior reviews that treat BCI hardware, AI decoding models, and pedagogical deployment as separate topics, this review develops an integrated cross-layer taxonomy linking hardware constraints, AI architecture requirements, and classroom deployment conditions. Emphasis is placed on the transition from cumbersome laboratory systems to wearable hybrid solutions combining electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), as well as textile sensors that offer a favorable trade-off between neurophysiological signal quality and mobility in real-world classroom settings. The review includes a detailed analysis of modern AI architectures, transformer-based models for processing non-stationary neural signals, and Siamese neural networks implementing a few-shot learning paradigm to address the calibration problem associated with new users. It further proposes a unified state-estimation framework integrating cognitive load, attention, and affect into a single formalization for closed-loop adaptive learning systems. The review concludes with a critical analysis of fundamental barriers to scalability, signal instability, mental state privacy issues, and the risk of a neurocognitive divide arising from unequal access to technology. The authors argue that the future of neuroeducation lies in the symbiotic interaction of humans and AI, supported by unified international standards and the convergence of BCI with large language models (LLM) for predictive communication.

paper_title: Aquagenic Syringeal Acrokeratoderma Successfully Managed with Topical Glycopyrronium: A Case and Review of the Literature
paper_abstract: Acquired aquagenic syringeal acrokeratoderma (ASA) is a rare dermatological disorder characterised by transient oedematous papules and palmar wrinkling following water exposure. Multiple treatment modalities have been described, however evidence supporting effective therapies is limited. We report a case of a 21-year-old Indian male with a 2-year history of painful palmar wrinkling, tingling, and stinging occurring approximately 15 minutes after water exposure, with associated pruritus and peeling following prolonged immersion. Clinical findings were consistent with acquired ASA, and investigations excluded systemic disease. Initial treatment with topical 20% aluminium chloride was discontinued because of excessive dryness. Subsequent treatment with topical glycopyrronium bromide 2% spray produced a 50% reduction in symptom severity without adverse effects, with sustained improvement over 1.5 years. This favourable response supports current evidence for a pathogenic role for eccrine gland dysfunction and sweating in ASA and suggests that epithelial transmembrane channelopathy with sweat leakage may contribute to disease development. Treatments targeting these pathways may therefore be effective strategies and topical glycopyrronium bromide can be a therapeutic consideration in ASA. Further studies are needed to validate these mechanisms and establish optimal management strategies.

paper_title: Residual Hepatocellular Carcinoma Risk After Bariatric Surgery: Fibrosis Regression, Metabolic Improvement, and Implications for Surveillance—A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Background and Objectives: Metabolic and bariatric surgery improves obesity and metabolic dys-function-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), but its effect on the residual risk of hepatocellu- lar carcinoma (HCC) is less clearly defined. This narrative review examines the relationship between postoperative metabolic improvement, fibrosis regression, and HCC risk, with particular attention to surveillance. Materials and Methods: A targeted literature search identified clinical studies, mechanistic investigations, and professional guidance relevant to bariatric surgery, MASLD, and HCC. Results: Randomized and paired-biopsy studies support improvement in steatohepatitis, whereas observational cohorts associate surgery with lower HCC occurrence and fewer major adverse liver outcomes. These findings address different endpoints and should not be treated as interchangeable evidence of cancer prevention. Advanced fibrosis can persist despite substantial weight loss and resolution of steatohepatitis. Conversely, the absolute postoperative HCC risk among patients with documented fibrosis regression remains insufficiently characterized. The available evidence does not establish a postoperative biochemical, elastographic, or histological threshold at which surveillance can safely be stopped in patients with established cirrhosis. Conclusion: Surveillance decisions should therefore remain anchored to the underlying liver disease, treatment eligibility, and applicable guidance rather than weight loss alone. Noncirrhotic advanced fibrosis requires individualized assessment because professional recommendations differ and evidence is limited. Future studies should report HCC separately from composite liver outcomes and evaluate risk according to baseline and postoperative fibrosis, metabolic trajectories, and surveillance exposure. Bariatric surgery may modify the course of liver disease, but metabolic improvement should not be equated with elimination of carcinogenic risk.

paper_title: Extension Services and the Social Sustainability Mission of Higher Education Institutions (HEIs): A Critical Integrative Review
paper_abstract: Higher education institutions (HEIs) are increasingly expected to contribute to sustainable development through research, instruction, and community engagement. However, contemporary higher education systems have become progressively research-oriented, prioritizing publication productivity, citation metrics, and institutional rankings. While these developments have expanded academic knowledge production, they have also contributed to a growing disconnect between knowledge generation and societal utilization. Within this context, extension services remain comparatively underprioritized despite their potential role in translating academic knowledge into meaningful community impact. This paper presents a critical integrative review of extension services in higher education, focusing on their conceptual evolution, institutional positioning, and contribution to the social sustainability mission of universities. The review examines how extension services have evolved from traditional technology-transfer and outreach models toward broader paradigms of community engagement, knowledge democratization, and sustainability-oriented development. It further analyzes the institutional marginalization of extension services within increasingly research-driven academic systems. Findings suggest that extension services remain insufficiently theorized and institutionally undervalued despite their critical role in promoting equitable knowledge access and community-centered development. The paper argues that extension services should be repositioned as central mechanisms through which HEIs translate academic knowledge into sustainable societal impact.

paper_title: When Coding Agents Outpace Review: Evaluating PRD-Driven Development in Mature Enterprise Repositories
paper_abstract: Coding agents increasingly undertake development tasks in mature enterprise repositories, yet existing benchmarks offer limited insight into whether they fulfill complete Product Requirement Documents (PRDs) and where delivery breaks down. Issue resolution and development from scratch leave incremental PRD fulfillment underexplored, while isolated tests provide incomplete evidence of business and integration requirements. We introduce PACE, a benchmark of 43 enterprise tasks with 750 expert-audited Code Points. It combines requirement reconstruction, criterion construction, and evidence-based evaluation to measure PRD fulfillment and connect delivery gaps to agent behavior. Across 11 model--scaffold configurations, most scores fall between 52.1 and 78.1; GPT-5.6-Sol achieves the highest complete-delivery rate of 14.0\%. Incomplete implementation and missing integration are the principal bottlenecks: producing individual components does not ensure a complete delivery. Evaluation achieves 95.2\% agreement with expert consensus, with lower case-level variation across judging records than repeated executions. Beyond model comparison, the benchmark provides actionable feedback for harness refinement: diagnosis guides targeted improvements, and successive harness releases raise mean performance from 59.4 to 63.0 using the same model and task suite. Code is available at https://github.com/TianqiLiu1/PACE-Bench.

paper_title: Leveraging Mental Models for Human-Centered Explanations: A Systematic Design Approach Illustrated by Explainable Fake Review Identification
paper_abstract: Explainable AI (XAI) often prioritizes model fidelity over user intelligibility, yielding explanations that satisfy technical transparency yet fail to support human sense-making. We propose a human-centered approach, MIND-X (Mental-model INtegrated Design for eXplainability), which aligns explanations with users' mental models, commonsense concepts, and judgment heuristics. Using fake review detection as a case study, we contribute: (1) a qualitative study (n=10) that elicits how people assess review credibility and produces an actionable, design-guiding taxonomy of perceptual cues; (2) a set of design principles that link those cues to explanation strategies and prompt LLMs to generate adaptive, language-based explanations; and (3) a quantitative evaluation (n=166) showing that these explanations offer distinct advantages over token-level transparency methods widely used in explainable text classification in terms of understandability, satisfaction, perceived trust, persuasiveness, and decision-making support. Rather than claiming general superiority, our evaluation illustrates how grounding explanations in users' everyday reasoning practices can produce more intelligible and context-sensitive accounts. Our findings advance human-centered explanation design beyond a mere "gloss of transparency," demonstrating that a mental-model-aligned design process can improve intelligibility and support accountability across user-centered explanation tasks.
comments: 38 pages, 10 figures, 8 tables. Keywords: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI); Human-centered AI; Mental models; Fake review detection; User-centered explanation design; Natural language explanations; Cognitive heuristics

paper_title: Towards Next-Generation Architectures of Large Language Models: A Survey
