We adopt the one-sided verification objective that maximizes the rejection rate of invalid solutions (TNR) under a constraint on the false-rejection rate of valid ones (FNR), making human review cost an explicit term to minimize. Drawing on the intuition that verifying a specific error can be easier than discovering one, we introduce OSVerify, an algorithmic framework that decouples error proposal from error validation. The error proposer searches for errors in solutions across different granularities by hierarchical decomposition, while the validator distinguishes substantial errors from minor or hallucinated ones. Experiments on competition- and research-level benchmarks show that OSVerify reduces the number of human reviews of invalid solutions by 46% on average compared to voting baselines under the same empirical low FNR constraint. Our post-training of the validator further improves the reduction to 57%. As high-impact real-world use cases, we apply OSVerify to identify errors in published research papers that are subsequently confirmed by the original authors and help resolve three Langlands open conjectures that are confirmed by experts, demonstrating its utility to facilitate human-AI research collaboration.

paper_title: Multiheme Cytochrome c7 Expansion Is a Phylum-Level Trait of the Candidate Phylum Kryptonia: A Survey of 22,307 Prokaryotic Genomes
paper_abstract: Background: Multiheme c-type cytochromes (MHCs) are the principal conduits of extracellular electron transfer (EET) in dissimilatory metal-reducing bacteria, yet their distribution across recently described candidate phyla remains poorly resolved. The cytochrome c7 family (triheme per core module) is a widespread MHC lineage whose phylum-level copy-number architecture has never been systematically surveyed. Methods: We scanned 22,307 prokaryotic genomes spanning candidate and established phyla with a dedicated c7-family profile HMM (E < 0.01), quantified per-genome copy numbers and CXXCH heme-binding motif loads, and benchmarked Kryptonia against Aquificota, DPANN, CPR, and a broad genomic background. Results: All 51 Kryptonia genomes encode c7 homologs, with a median of 15 copies per genome (max 19; 100% of genomes ≥5 copies; 88% ≥10) — the highest median per-genome dosage of any surveyed clade. By contrast, the largest Aquificota family (Aquificaceae) encodes a median of 1 copy, DPANN a median of 0 (max 6), and 98.9% of 20,217 background genomes carry fewer than 5. Kryptonia c7 proteins are also enriched in large MHCs: 49% carry ≥9 CXXCH motifs, versus 15–25% in CPR/DPANN. Canonical and divergent (novel) copies co-occur in 49/51 genomes, indicating a mixed repertoire rather than fixation of a single variant. Conclusions: High-copy, mixed-composition c7 repertoires are a phylum-level trait of Kryptonia rather than an isolate-specific anomaly, positioning this candidate phylum as a previously unrecognized reservoir of multiheme electron-transfer architecture.

paper_title: A Comprehensive Survey on LLM-Guided Evolutionary Search
paper_abstract: Large Language Model-guided Evolutionary Search (LLM-ES), exemplified by AlphaEvolve, has recently demonstrated impressive performance in solving goal-driven problems with extremely large and complex search spaces. Unlike conventional LLM approaches based on single-shot or few-shot sampling, LLM-ES introduces population-based evolution to iteratively generate more novel and higher-quality solutions. Compared with traditional Evolutionary Computing algorithms, LLM-ES treats LLMs as semantic variation operators. This design extends the search space from low-dimensional vectors to expressive and language-defined structures such as code and programs. Meanwhile, the rich prior knowledge embedded in LLMs significantly improves the efficiency of evolutionary search in complex solution spaces. As a result, LLM-ES effectively exploits the test-time scaling capability of LLMs and achieves state-of-the-art performance in many open-ended problems. In this survey, we provide a systematic overview of this emerging field. We first formalize the problem setting and the general pipeline of LLM-ES. We then review existing works from several key perspectives, including population design, prompt builder, LLM model selection, evaluation design, and exploration-exploitation control. Finally, we summarize representative applications and discuss open challenges and future research directions.

paper_title: Applications of Quartz Sand in Petroleum Production and Engineering Material Selection: A Comprehensive Review
paper_abstract: Quartz sand is used throughout oil and gas well engineering, including hydraulic fracturing, wellbore sand control, high-temperature cementing and produced-water treatment, but each use imposes distinct require-ments on particle size, morphology, strength, reactivity and cleanliness. Following the performance chain from mineral source, washing and size classification, storage and transport, slurry injection and fracture placement to long-term service, this review discusses proppant transport and settling, bridging and bed-load migration, breakage and wall embedment under closure stress, fines migration, fracture-fluid residues, mul-tiphase and non-Darcy flow, stress cycling and time-dependent damage. Natural quartz sand, pre-cured and curable resin-coated sands, ceramic proppants and mixed proppants are compared. Material selection should be based on target-well long-term conductivity tests and life-cycle economics. The review also considers gravel packing, where grain-size matching to formation sand, screen compatibility and packing completeness are critical, and high-temperature well cementing, where finely ground silica regulates the calcium-to-silicon ra-tio of hydration products and mitigates strength retrogression. API Std 19C and ISO 13503-2:2024 provide the basic characterization framework, whereas ISO 13503-5:2006 can organize long-term conductivity compari-son but does not provide an absolute in-situ conductivity. A project-level test matrix, minimum reporting set and batch-traceability loop are proposed for resource assessment, product development, procurement and field verification.

paper_title: Biomedical Applications of Nanotechnology in Chronic Kidney Disease: A Thematic and Translational Review with Supporting Bibliometric Analysis
paper_abstract: Background: Nanotechnology has expanded biomedical applications in chronic kidney disease (CKD), including diagnostics, monitoring, targeted therapy, and extracorporeal management. However, heterogeneity in materials, experimental models, and translational development complicates assessment of clinical progress. This review characterized major CKD nanotechnology applications and their documented translational stages, supported by complementary bibliometric analysis. Methods: English-language original studies indexed in PubMed/MEDLINE between July 1, 2021, and July 1, 2026, were organized into 11 overlapping thematic categories and classified according to their highest documented translational stage. Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny characterized publication, journal, institutional, and geographic patterns, while VOSviewer analyzed MeSH term co-occurrence. Results: Of 288 records identified, 160 studies across 91 journals were included. The most frequent categories were nanodiagnostics and biosensors (53 studies), nanotherapy for renal fibrosis (51), kidney-targeted drug delivery (28), and redox nanomedicine, inflammation, and oxidative stress (27). Diagnostic platforms more frequently reached human-sample validation or early clinical evaluation, whereas therapeutic approaches remained predominantly preclinical. Extracorporeal nanotechnologies were largely experimental, with limited human-sample evaluation. The 10 most productive journals accounted for 55 studies (34.4%), illustrating the concentration of publications within a multidisciplinary field. Conclusions: CKD nanomedicine exhibits substantial technological diversity but uneven translational development. Progress toward clinical implementation requires standardized physicochemical characterization, reproducibility, independent validation, long-term safety assessment, manufacturing scalability, and rigorous comparisons with established standards of care using clinically meaningful outcomes.

paper_title: A Systematic Review of Impacts of Land Policies on Historically Disadvantaged Individuals in South Africa
paper_abstract: Introduction: Land policies are frequently presented as instruments for correcting colonial, racial, feudal and elite‐concentrated land inequality. Across the supplied literature, however, formal redistribution, restitution, recognition and titling do not consistently produce secure tenure or improved socioeconomic conditions for historically disadvantaged populations. This systematic review examined how land reform, redistribution, restitution, tenure regularization and titling relate to socioeconomic impacts and tenure security, while identifying enabling conditions, risks and implementation barriers. Methods: The researcher‐selected databases and information sources were Google Scholar, PubMed (MEDLINE) and ERIC. The eligibility protocol restricted publication years to 2025–2026. The exact calendar date of search execution was not recorded in the verified identification provenance; this is distinct from the publication‐year eligibility range. Google Scholar, PubMed (MEDLINE) and ERIC were searched using the supplied Boolean strategy for English peer‐ reviewed studies published between 2025 and 2026. Results: Land reform was consistently framed as a project of distributive and reparative justice, but redistribution was constrained by political instability, elite accommodation, weak administrative capacity, regulatory overlap and inadequate conflict resolution. Formal recognition frequently protected only partial or selected rights. Socioeconomic benefits depended on complementary water, infrastructure, inputs, services, livelihood support and recognition of local knowledge. Poorly planned reform, conservation restrictions and resettlement generated displacement, livelihood disruption, food insecurity and conflict. Participation, inclusion, accessible information, accountability and free, prior and informed consent were recurrent enabling conditions. Discussion/Conclusion: Land policies can advance justice and livelihood security, but their effects are conditional rather than automatic. Effective reform requires institutional capacity, substantive redistribution, inclusive tenure recognition and integrated socioeconomic support.

paper_title: Effects of Endosymbionts on Arthropod Behavior: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
paper_abstract: Facultative endosymbionts living within arthropod cells are known to affect several aspects their hosts’ behavior. Here we synthesize studies that measure effects of endosymbionts on arthropod behavioral traits, ranging from effects on host activity and feeding to mating and multitrophic interactions with predators and parasitoids. Our systematic review of the literature identified 70 laboratory studies that compared behavioral traits between arthropod populations where the endosymbiont was either present or absent. In a meta-analysis of 799 comparisons (639 Hedges’ g effect sizes and 160 log of odds ratios for binomial data) across different endosymbiont species and behavioral categories, we found that the presence of facultative endosymbionts tended to provide benefits to mating but costs to feeding, while for many other traits endosymbionts had no overall effect or patterns depended on the endosymbiont or host species. Measured effects of endosymbionts tended to be larger when the genetic background of the strains was not controlled. We discuss challenges with assessing effects of endosymbionts on arthropod behavior, identify avenues for future studies and highlight implications for field releases of arthropod lines carrying endosymbionts for pest and pathogen control.

paper_title: Trustworthy Federated Intrusion Detection for the Future Internet: A Critical Review and Evaluation Framework
paper_abstract: Federated intrusion detection for the Future Internet must operate across heterogeneous devices, distributed telemetry, changing traffic patterns, and adversarial clients. This critical structured review synthesizes a targeted corpus of 37 publications and standards, including 20 Future Internet articles, coded on six methodological evidence dimensions using a transparent ordinal rubric. Federated-learning relevance received the highest mean coverage score (3.32/5; 24 of 37 records scored at least 3), followed by reproducibility (2.89/5; 19 of 37). Evidence for robustness (1.19/5; 10 of 37), generalization (1.00/5; 7 of 37), explainability (1.27/5; 7 of 37), and deployment realism (1.59/5; 10 of 37) was markedly sparser. Only five records scored at least 3 on both robustness and generalization. These results describe the methods addressed in a purposefully selected literature corpus, not the performance of deployed detection systems. Based on the observed coverage gaps, we propose a reproducible evaluation framework encompassing non-independent and identically distributed federation, disjoint and open-set testing, poisoning and backdoor attacks, leakage auditing, explanation stability, and edge-resource measurements. A supplementary Excel workbook separates original source-level coding from formula-linked analyses and sensitivity checks. Trustworthy federated intrusion detection should be evaluated through this joint systems-level evidence rather than closed-world predictive accuracy alone.

paper_title: Social Relationships in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Profound Shifts and New Challenges—An Integrative Literature Review
paper_abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) has moved from a tool for information retrieval to a partner in conversation, advice, and emotional support. This integrative review examines whether that shift is reshaping friendship and other social bonds. Drawing on relationship science, human–machine communication research, surveys, experiments, longitudinal panels, randomized trials, and meta-analyses published through September 2026, including emerging evidence from Arab societies, the review develops the Responsiveness–Reciprocity Bridge Model to explain why conversational AI can relieve loneliness in the moment yet fail to build the relational capital that sustains people over time. A substantial minority of adolescents and young adults already turn to chatbots when they feel sad, anxious, or lonely, and short-term interactions with companion systems can reduce loneliness about as much as talking with another person, largely because users feel heard. These gains do not establish that synthetic ties can replace human friendship. Close relationships require mutual need, sacrifice, shared history, and practical solidarity that chatbots do not provide; in a randomized experiment, a human peer outperformed a highly supportive chatbot, and longitudinal and large-sample studies associate intensive, companionship-oriented use with greater loneliness and lower well-being. In Arab contexts, culturally aligned and human-guided digital tools show promise, but claims that AI is widely replacing traditional friends are not supported by comparable prevalence research. The central implication is balance: AI can widen access to support, but only if it is designed, governed, and used as a bridge to human relationships rather than as a substitute for them.

paper_title: Family Socioeconomic Status and Child and Adolescent Developmental Outcomes: A Review and Meta-Analysis
paper_abstract: Lower family socioeconomic status (SES) is widely linked to poorer child development, but the magnitude of the association varies across outcomes and samples. To synthesise correlational evidence on SES and externalizing/antisocial behaviour, internalizing/depressive symptoms, and language/literacy in children and adolescents. Multiple databases including Scopus, Web of Science and PubMed/MEDLINE were searched. Reports were screened against a pre-specified protocol (age ≤ 10 years; income/SES exposure; positive developmental outcomes), and effects were extracted as SES–outcome correlations (Fisher z). A post-hoc synthesis of the reported outcomes was undertaken with random-effects models, subgroup analysis by outcome domain, meta-regression, sensitivity analysis and funnel-plot/Egger tests using Stata version 17. 12 studies were included. Eight studies examined relations with externalizing outcomes (r = 0.04, 95% CI: 0.11, 0.03), and 6 studies examined relations with internalizing outcomes (r = 0.04, 95% CI: 0.12, 0.05). Language/literacy outcomes showed positive relations to SES (r = 0.24-0.46; exploratory pooled r = 0.38, 95% CI: 0.26, 0.49), with outcome domain accounting for significant between-subgroup heterogeneity. Mainly adolescents, family SES was weakly and inconsistently related to externalising and internalising problems, and prediction intervals were large. Language/literacy had a more robust positive SES gradient but only two small independent samples.

paper_title: The Spectrum of Penetrating Craniocerebral Injuries in Pakistan: A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Background: Although penetrating craniocerebral injuries (PCIs) are rare, they can be extremely serious and are linked with a high level of neurological morbidity and mortality. In Pakistan, published work mainly consists of individual case reports and small case series, with wide variation in mechanisms, anatomical paths, radiological findings, surgical methods, and outcomes. This narrative review aims to bring together the existing literature on various types of penetrating brain and craniocerebral injuries in Pakistan and describe their clinical, radiological, and management characteristics. Methods: Studies were screened against predefined eligibility criteria, with an emphasis on injuries caused by penetrating objects, including unusual low-velocity foreign bodies. Relevant information was extracted on the mechanism and circumstances of injury; clinical and neurological presentation; anatomical entry site and trajectory; depth and location of the foreign body; radiological characteristics; surgical management; and postoperative outcomes and complications. Results: Six Pakistani publications met the eligibility criteria and were included in the narrative synthesis. The reported injuries demonstrated considerable heterogeneity in the type of penetrating object, anatomical entry site, trajectory, and intracranial location. Penetration occurred through different cranial and facial regions, with foreign bodies traversing cortical and deeper intracranial structures in some cases. Clinical presentation ranged from relatively preserved neurological status to severe neurological impairment, depending on the trajectory and structures involved. Computed tomography was central to defining the entry site, trajectory, depth, retained foreign body, and associated intracranial injuries. Despite the severity of some injuries, selected patients had favorable neurological outcomes, while complications included infection, neurological deficits, and other procedure- or injury-related sequelae. Conclusion: Pakistani literature demonstrates that PCIs are clinically diverse and require individualized assessment based on the entry site, trajectory, depth, and anatomical relationship of the foreign body to critical intracranial structures. However, evidence remains limited to a small number of case-based publications, highlighting the need for systematic reporting and larger multicenter studies to define better injury patterns, management strategies, complications, and long-term outcomes of PCIs in Pakistan.

paper_title: Error Enhancement in Physical Rehabilitation: From Motor Learning Theory to Robotic Neurorehabilitation– A Comprehensive Review
paper_abstract: Error enhancement (EE), also referred to as error augmentation (EA), represents a distinctive ap-proach to motor rehabilitation in which errors are not minimized but deliberately magnified in a controlled manner. The underlying premise is derived from contemporary theories of motor learning and sensorimotor adaptation: when the nervous system detects a discrepancy between the intended and actual consequences of a movement, this error provides a powerful teaching signal that can modify subsequent motor commands. Robotic systems make it possible to manipulate this error precisely by applying externally generated forces that deviate the limb from its intended trajectory. This review examines the theoretical basis of error enhancement, its development as a rehabilitation strategy in particular attention is given to studies conducted in healthy individuals and stroke survivors. The available evidence is then considered in relation to sensorimotor inte-gration, virtual reality, constraint-induced movement therapy, and the Bobath concept. Finally, the emergence of the BioXtreme/deXtreme robotic platform is discussed as a translational development that combines robotic force-field manipulation, three-dimensional movement, virtual reality and adaptive error enhancement. Although the evidence remains preliminary and larger controlled trials are required, error enhancement provides a compelling framework for converting movement error from a problem to be suppressed into a signal that can actively drive motor adaptation and rehabilitation.

paper_title: Long Non-Coding RNAs in Immune Thrombocytopenia: A Narrative Review of Pathogenesis and Clinical Implications
paper_abstract: Background/Objectives: Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) is an autoimmune disease characterized by increased platelet destruction and insufficient platelet production. Accurate diagnosis, prognostic assessment, and treatment selection remain challenging. Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) regulate immune responses and may contribute to ITP pathogenesis. This review examines lncRNA expression in ITP and its potential diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic relevance. Methods: We reviewed English-language literature published between 1994 and 2026 using PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar. We examined studies of specific lncRNAs in ITP, focusing on their expression differences and potential diagnostic and therapeutic implications. Re-sults: The studies examined HCP5, NEAT1, lnc-DC, IFNG-AS1, MEG3, GAS5, MALAT1, and THRIL. Findings suggest these lncRNAs may contribute to ITP pathogenesis and serve as candidate diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers. Some were reported as independent predictors of poor prognosis or were associated with glucocorticoid responsiveness. Potential applications include distinguishing primary from secondary ITP, informing patient selection for splenectomy, and identifying therapeutic targets. These applications remain investigational. Conclusions: Research on lncRNAs provides insight into autoimmune mechanisms underlying ITP and may support improvements in diagnosis, prognostic assessment, and individualized treatment. Although several lncRNAs show promise as biomarkers and therapeutic targets, further research, clinical validation, and methodological standardization are needed before routine clinical implementation.

paper_title: A Systematic Review of Crash Causes and Safety Trends in Automated Driving Systems and Advanced Driver Assistance Systems
paper_abstract: As Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) and Automated Driving Systems (ADS) technologies become more prevalent, evaluating their safety performance in complex, real-world environments has emerged as a critical research priority. This study presents a systematic literature review of crashes involving vehicles equipped with ADAS and ADS. Using the PRISMA methodology, this review analyzed 51 peer-reviewed articles and books published between 2018 and 2025. Articles were identified through comprehensive searches of ScienceDirect, TRID, and the Transportation Research Record. The selected studies were organized into five thematic categories: safety and crash characteristics, human interaction and user behavior, testing tools and simulations, cybersecurity and perception risks, and policy and governance. Findings reveal that while AV technologies show promise in reducing crash severity and frequency, performance is highly context-dependent, affected by roadway geometry, weather, system limitations, and user behavior. ADAS-related crashes are more common on highways and often involve human error, whereas ADS crashes are more likely in urban settings and linked to system disengagements. The review also highlights significant gaps in data availability, standardized evaluation protocols, and human-machine interaction research. Despite growing literature, many studies rely heavily on simulations and legacy datasets, limiting generalizability. To support safer AV deployment, future research must prioritize real-world testing and user trust frameworks deployment strategies. This review offers a knowledge base to guide policymakers, researchers, and industry stakeholders in advancing the development and regulation of vehicle automation technologies.

paper_title: Does Sexual Trauma Accelerate Biological Aging? A Narrative Review of Epigenetic, Cellular, Endocrine, Inflammatory and Metabolic Pathways
paper_abstract: Survivors of sexual violence carry a disproportionate burden of age-related morbidity, including cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes and inflammatory conditions, raising the possibility that sexual trauma accelerates the biology of aging rather than acting solely through psychological distress or health behaviors. This narrative review synthesizes translational, epidemiological and biomarker evidence across five mechanistic domains. Epigenetically, posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is associated with accelerated DNA-methylation age, most consistently on the mortality-calibrated GrimAge clock, whereas meta-analytic evidence for cumulative childhood adversity on first- and second-generation clocks is weak. At the cellular level, severe childhood sexual abuse is associated with shorter leukocyte telomeres in several, though not all, studies, and PTSD with telomere attrition, T-cell senescence and oxidative DNA damage. Endocrinologically, childhood sexual abuse produces enduring hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis sensitization and earlier pubertal maturation in girls. Inflammatory evidence is the most robust: childhood maltreatment prospectively predicts adult C-reactive protein, and PTSD is consistently associated with elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines. Metabolically, PTSD is associated with a high prevalence of metabolic syndrome, and childhood sexual abuse with obesity and type 2 diabetes in women. Glucocorticoid-FKBP5-NF-κB signaling and allostatic load emerge as bridges between domains, and we propose an integrated six-step model. Causal inference remains limited by retrospective trauma assessment, confounding by co-occurring adversity and scarce trauma-type-specific analyses. Priorities include prospective, sexual-trauma-specific multi-omic studies and trials testing whether trauma-focused, anti-inflammatory or metabolic interventions can slow the pace of biological aging in survivors.

paper_title: How Well Do LLMs Perform in Peer Review? Evidence from Finance and Accounting
paper_abstract: Referees increasingly use large language models (LLMs), while finance and accounting journals disagree about whether to allow it. We ask which part of a referee's job the models can do. GPT-4o, whose training data end before the 2024 conference season, referees the papers presented at the 2024 AFA and NBER finance meetings, and we compare its verdicts with publication in the top-three finance journals over the next two years. Papers the model scores one standard deviation higher are 44\% more likely to be published, net of author reputation. The result is not driven by look-ahead bias, as the model does not recall the outcomes. The information comes from its judgements of correctness and exposition. Its judgements of originality and significance carry none, and a referee guide that stresses importance does not help. The split between correctness and contribution holds for accounting papers and for a newer model, GPT-5. LLMs can check whether research is right, but not whether it matters. The technical check can go to the model, while the judgement of contribution stays with people.

paper_title: Comparing GenAI to Machine Learning and Manual Review for eDiscovery
paper_abstract: Keeling et al. [Keeling2026Generative] report on a case study recently conducted by Redgrave LLP in which they assert that Relativity's Generative AI Review tool (aiR) achieved 88% recall while Relativity Assisted Learning (RAL), its machine-learning tool, achieved 64% recall. These results are not comparable because the methods employed have different objectives, because of inter-assessor disagreement, and because they represent different recall-precision and cost-benefit trade-offs. Our analysis of the Redgrave data indicates that, when these differences are taken into account, aiR and manual review are comparable. Furthermore, established machine-learning models employing Continuous Active Learning (CAL) and Scalable Continuous Active Learning (S-CAL) show state-of-the-art effectiveness, and superior efficiency, when trained only on a sample of 2,000 first-pass-reviewer responsiveness determinations.

paper_title: Evaluating Security Claims in LLM Systems: A Survey of Adversarial Attacks and Defenses
paper_abstract: Attack success rates alone do not establish the security of large language model (LLM) systems because results depend on the attacker, deployment conditions, and measured consequence. This survey complements existing attack and defense taxonomies by examining what individual experiments actually support. We pair a threat model describing attacker capabilities and objectives with a defense model specifying observable information, security functions, and enforceable responses. An attack-defense assurance matrix determines whether an evaluation addresses the conditions relevant to a stated security claim. A bounded claim grammar also records the attacker, system version, consequence, cost, evaluation oracle, and other conditions that limit the result. An evidence ladder organizes empirical requirements for a fixed security claim and threat model without ranking papers or defenses. We apply the framework across model behavior, retrieval and memory, agents and tools, supply chains, privacy, availability, and serving infrastructure. The resulting synthesis helps researchers and practitioners distinguish demonstrated protection from untested conditions, compare results under matched assumptions, and design evaluations that measure the security consequences relevant to deployment.

paper_title: Summer Compound Hot-Drought Extreme Events over Northwest China: A Review of Recent Studies
paper_abstract: Under global warming, compound extreme events threaten ecosystems and socio-economic systems more than individual extremes. As a typical arid and semi-arid region, Northwest China has witnessed continuous increases in concurrent summer hot and drought conditions, threatening regional water security, agriculture and ecological stability. Based on observation and reanalysis data since 1961, this paper reviews recent progress on the definition, spatiotemporal variation and formation mechanisms of Summer Compound Hot-Drought Extreme Events (CHDEE) in Northwest China. Results show that the fusion scheme of daily drought and heatwave indicators, as well as the Copula joint probability framework, perform well in regional CHDEE detection. CHDEE frequency has increased significantly, with a pronounced acceleration since the late 1990s. Spatially, CHDEE show a pattern of high values in the west and low values in the east. Affected areas expand from the arid core to the northern margins and southern high-altitude regions. CHDEE are controlled by multi-scale factors: the westerly circulation, the East Asian summer monsoon and the thermal forcing of the Tibetan Plateau. The positive soil moisture–temperature feedback is the key amplification mechanism. Current studies still lack unified definitions, and the mechanisms over complex terrain remain unclear. Future work should strengthen multi-source data fusion and develop physics-informed AI prediction methods.

paper_title: Organic Residues and Cultural Memory: A Systematic Review of Archaeochemical Evidence in Reconstructing Ancient Foodways and Ritual Practices
paper_abstract: Archaeochemical investigations of organic residues have significantly advanced the reconstruction of ancient lifeways by providing molecular evidence of subsistence strategies, ritual behavior, technological practices, and socio-symbolic systems. This study presents a systematic review of archaeochemical scholarship published between 2010 and 2024, synthesizing empirical findings from forty-five peer-reviewed studies retrieved from Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar. Guided by PRISMA 2020 protocols, the review evaluates archaeological materials analyzed, analytical techniques employed, residue categories identified, and interpretive frameworks linking biomolecular signatures to cultural memory and religious practice. The findings demonstrate the methodological dominance of chromatographic and spectrometric approaches, particularly gas chromatography–mass spectrometry, liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry, isotope ratio mass spectrometry, and spectroscopic screening techniques. Lipid biomarkers remain foundational for reconstructing subsistence systems and dietary transitions, while increasing use of proteomic and isotopic analyses has expanded interpretive capacity toward ritual consumption practices, technological knowledge transmission, and spatial organization of domestic activities. Organic compounds such as fatty acids, fermentation markers, terpenoids, nicotine alkaloids, and resinous substances emerge as key proxies for interpreting culinary traditions, ceremonial behavior, and symbolic technological practices. The review highlights a disciplinary shift toward multi-proxy analytical integration and micro-contextual approaches that enhance the reliability of cultural reconstruction. The synthesis suggests that organic residues may be interpreted as biochemical indicators of repeated cultural practices preserved within archaeological materials. Future research directions include the development of comparative residue databases, high-resolution analytical techniques, and interdisciplinary collaboration to support more holistic reconstructions of ancient socio-cultural systems.

paper_title: Does Depression Phenotype Predict Antidepressant Response? A Transdiagnostic Review of Phenotype-Specific Antidepressant Efficacy
paper_abstract: Major depressive disorder is one of the most prevalent and disabling conditions worldwide, yet fewer than one-third of patients achieve remission with the first antidepressant prescribed. The clinical phenotypes codified across successive editions of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM) — melancholic, atypical, anxious, and psychotic forms of depression — were proposed, in part, because they were thought to predict differential response to specific drug classes. This narrative review evaluates the evidence for phenotype-specific antidepressant efficacy across the full depressive spectrum, including treatment-resistant depression as a longitudinal phenotype and the transdiagnostic reformulations advanced by the Research Domain Criteria initiative. Historical controlled trials demonstrated genuine but circumscribed phenotype–drug interactions, most notably the preferential response of atypical depression to monoamine oxidase inhibitors relative to tricyclic antidepressants. However, contemporary large-scale effectiveness data from the Sequenced Treatment Alternatives to Relieve Depression (STAR*D) and the International Study to Predict Optimized Treatment in Depression (iSPOT-D) trials do not support subtype-based antidepressant selection. Much of the apparent predictive value of melancholic status is confounded by illness severity and placebo responsiveness, while data-driven re-analyses have failed to biologically validate the DSM-defined subtypes. Anxious depression and treatment-resistant depression robustly identify poorer outcomes but do not yet point clinicians toward specific drug classes. Weighing the totality of evidence, categorical depression phenotypes have limited utility in predicting antidepressant response; the most clinically reproducible signal is severity-dependent drug–placebo separation, and the most promising route to precision prescribing lies in transdiagnostic, multimodal biosignatures and machine-learning approaches.

paper_title: Differential Privacy Protected Preference Alignment on Survey Derived Data
paper_abstract: Preference alignment enables language models to better reflect human values, but the preference data contains sensitive information, especially when derived from surveys about political beliefs, social norms, religion, gender attitudes, and cultural values. This paper studies privacy-preserving alignment on questionnaire-derived data from the World Values Survey, where supervision takes the form of ordinal labels rather than standard pairwise rankings. Existing efforts mainly focus on general privacy protections upon model training, while data-specific methods for survey data remain unexplored. We first show the vulnerability of aligned models, then formulate the task as rating prediction and introduce label differential privacy. Building on this formulation, we construct a differential private pipeline utilizing three privacy mechanisms: randomized response, exponential mechanism, and DP-SGD. Experiments show that simple label-level mechanisms outperform gradient-level methods, and proper aggregation function for preprocessing also make large contribution. The new fine-grained private comparison motivates explorations toward language model alignment with formal privacy guarantees.

paper_title: A Survey of Flow Matching in Reinforcement Learning
paper_abstract: Flow Matching (FM) has recently emerged as a principled and efficient generative modeling framework for reinforcement learning (RL), enabling expressive, multimodal policy parameterizations via deterministic probability transport. Compared to diffusion-based policies that rely on stochastic denoising chains, FM uses sampling based on ordinary differential equations (ODEs), with learned velocity fields, which can substantially reduce inference latency and simplify the incorporation of RL objectives. As research in flow-based RL rapidly accelerates across offline continuous control, online fine-tuning, and foundation model alignment, the literature has become highly fragmented. In this survey, we provide a comprehensive taxonomy of flow-matching approaches in reinforcement learning. We organize the literature along two axes: the target distribution being modeled (e.g., action policies, value critics, transition dynamics) and the mechanism of RL signal integration (e.g., energy-weighted regression, flow-based policy gradients, and group relative policy optimization). Furthermore, we survey emerging frontiers such as discrete and non-Euclidean action spaces, provide a systematic comparative analysis against Gaussian and diffusion baselines, and outline critical open problems. Ultimately, this survey serves as a foundational roadmap for the next generation of generative reinforcement learning and alignment.
comments: 52 pages. Published in Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR), 2026. Survey Certification. Reviewed on OpenReview: https://openreview.net/forum?id=P6e5IC4gPe

paper_title: Review Rarely Beats the Stronger Model: Separating Verification from Capability Transfer in LLM Pipelines
paper_abstract: Qwen3-8B reviewing Llama-3.1-8B in math adds 33.2 points, yet Qwen3-8B alone is 6.4 points more accurate than the result. Reviewing another model's answer is usually judged by its gain over the generator. We show that this confuses verification, which adds accuracy beyond either model alone, with capability transfer, where a stronger reviewer supplies answers it could have given on its own. Measured against the stronger model alone, across 48 pairs of 12 open-weight models (3B to 72B) in math, knowledge, code and reasoning, review beats it in only 9 of 96 review directions, and does worse the larger the capability gap. The reason is anchoring: the reviewer mostly follows the generator, discarding its own correct answers. Review costs 2.6 to 2.8 times as much as the stronger model alone, while a selector using the same two calls is 2.7 to 4.2 points more accurate than review and cheaper. Studies of verification should report the stronger model alone, not only the gain over the generator.

paper_title: Security in LLM-Assisted Coding: A Systematic Literature Review
paper_abstract: Large Language Models accelerate software development but introduce severe security vulnerabilities. This systematic review investigates security risks in automated coding, benchmark limitations, and the role of human developers. Findings indicate that models frequently generate insecure code and faulty patches due to training data biases. Additionally, the models themselves are susceptible to direct attacks. Current evaluation methods suffer from data contamination and lack robust security metrics. Consequently, human oversight remains essential. Safer integration of automation will require more security-aware model architectures, stronger security-specific benchmarks, and more effective human-AI collaboration frameworks to mitigate these systemic risks.
comments: 35 pages Accepted for publication in ACM Computing Surveys (CSUR). A copy of the formal acceptance letter can be verified via the publisher's portal or provided to moderators upon request

paper_title: From Acoustic Sensing to Physical Actions: A Comprehensive Survey of Security Risks in Edge-Deployed Audio LLM-Based Agents
paper_abstract: Audio Large Language Models (Audio LLMs) are embedded in agents for smart homes, vehicles, wearables, and embodied systems, where acoustic inputs can propagate from perception into persistent state and consequential execution. This setting extends security analysis beyond model behavior to the system conditions that determine how acoustic inputs can influence agent behavior and external actions. Existing surveys examine acoustic security, LLM-based agents, and edge deployment in isolation, leaving their security interactions in deployed Audio LLM-based agents insufficiently characterized. This survey introduces an Acoustic Sensing-to-Action (S2A) system model that traces these security implications along the path from acoustic sensing to external execution, while accounting for edge-cloud runtime and lifecycle transformation. We use the model to synthesize attacks, defenses, and evaluation methods across the acoustic, agent, and edge-system literature. The synthesis shows that security gaps can emerge within components and at the transitions between stages, where protections developed for one stage do not necessarily provide end-to-end assurance in the deployed system. These findings motivate security evaluation that follows acoustic influence from sensing to action across persistent state, system boundaries, and changing deployment conditions in real-world agents.

paper_title: Designing Artificial Intelligence Decision Support for Periodontal Care in Kazakhstan: A Three-Stakeholder Cross-Sectional Survey of Dentists, Primary Care Physicians and Patients
paper_abstract: Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) tools for periodontal diagnosis are proliferating, yet little is known about what clinicians and patients in Central Asia expect from such systems. We elicited requirements for an AI-enabled periodontal decision-support system from three stakeholder groups in Kazakhstan and examined which patient-reported risk factors are associated with self-reported signs of periodontal disease. Methods: A cross-sectional online survey (July–September 2026) enrolled 33 dentists, 91 primary health care (PHC) physicians and medical specialists, and 455 patients with periodontal disease. Proportions were reported with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CI); groups were compared with Fisher’s exact, χ², Mann–Whitney and Kruskal–Wallis tests with effect sizes; multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with self-reported periodontal signs. Results: Dentists prioritised automation of history-taking (81.8%) and visual gingival assessment (72.7%), and named early gingivitis diagnosis as the stage where AI is most needed (69.7%). Only human-controlled autonomy levels were chosen; the most frequently cited barrier was the absence of a legal framework and liability insurance (60.6%), and dentists with >5 years of experience more often demanded mandatory verification or a prohibition of full autonomy (exact p = 0.045; Cramér’s V = 0.54). PHC physicians considered early gingivitis screening their most effective contribution (80.2%) but cited insufficient competence as the main barrier (53.8%). Self-reported periodontal signs were present in 49.0% of patients and were independently associated with high stress (adjusted odds ratio 2.11; 95% CI 1.14–3.89) and a positive family history (1.61; 1.02–2.55); six symptom items did not form a reliable scale (Cronbach’s α = 0.56). Conclusions: Stakeholders in Kazakhstan favour a low-autonomy, clinician-verified AI system focused on early gingivitis detection, interprofessional data sharing and clearly regulated accountability. These requirements provide an evidence base for the design and governance of periodontal AI in emerging health systems.

paper_title: From Trajectories to Experience: A Survey of Experience-Driven LLM Agents
paper_abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can plan, use tools, and recover from errors within a task, yet many carry little from one task to the next and repeat mistakes they have already resolved. The root cause is a lack of experience accumulation: trajectories record what failed and how the agent recovered, but this information is seldom turned into guidance for later tasks. Research on this capability spans reflection, agent memory, workflow learning, and skill acquisition, but these lines describe similar content in different terms and lack a common account of experience itself, leaving basic questions open: what counts as experience, how it should be accumulated, used, and revised, and how to tell whether it improves later behavior. This survey addresses these questions with a unified framework. We define agent experience as action-guiding information grounded in task trajectories and retained to guide later episodes where it applies, whether as a trajectory precedent, a semantic lesson, or a reusable procedure. We focus on explicitly accessible experience, including its use as a training signal for internalization into model parameters. We describe each unit of experience by its guidance, applicability conditions, execution evidence, and reliability evaluation, so that memory entries, workflows, and skills become directly comparable, and follow experience through four lifecycle functions---formation, organization, utilization, and maintenance---that determine how it is accumulated, used, and revised. To judge reported gains, we distinguish three improvement claims---fixed experience reuse, feedback-driven sustained improvement, and improvement of the learning mechanism---by the evidence each requires. Current studies most clearly support fixed experience reuse, chiefly on tasks with tests or reference answers; evidence for the other two claims remains partial. Our analysis yields recommendations for seven application settings and a central design principle: keep guidance connected to its applicability conditions and to the evidence that supports or challenges it. Finally, we outline eight open problems, from learning with human expert records to testing whether gains accumulate, toward agents whose improvement is cumulative, transferable, and correctable.

paper_title: <span data-teams="true">Digital Transformation and the Adoption of Strategic Management Accounting Among Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises in Soweto, South Africa: A Literature Review
paper_abstract: The rapid advancement of digital technologies has transformed the operational and strategic landscape of Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (SMEs), creating opportunities to improve organisational performance through digitally enabled Strategic Management Accounting (SMA). While traditional management accounting primarily supports operational control and historical financial reporting, SMA extends this role by integrating financial and non-financial information to facilitate strategic planning, competitive positioning, and long-term decision-making. The emergence of cloud computing, artificial intelligence, enterprise resource planning systems, big data analytics, blockchain, and mobile accounting has significantly enhanced the ability of SMEs to generate timely, accurate, and strategic information. Despite these opportunities, the adoption of digitally enabled SMA remains uneven, particularly among township-based SMEs operating in resource-constrained environments such as Soweto, South Africa. Existing literature indicates that organisational limitations, technological barriers, infrastructural deficiencies, regulatory uncertainty, and inadequate managerial capabilities continue to constrain digital transformation within SMEs. Furthermore, much of the existing research has focused on large organisations and developed economies, resulting in limited understanding of how digital transformation influences SMA adoption within township businesses. This literature review critically synthesises current scholarly evidence regarding Strategic Management Accounting, digital transformation, theoretical explanations for technology adoption, and the organisational factors influencing digitally enabled SMA implementation among SMEs. The review further identifies major research gaps and proposes future research directions that contribute to both theory and practice by providing a context-specific understanding of digital transformation and strategic accounting within South African township economies.

paper_title: Keeping the Core, Adapting the Periphery: Structured Comparative Review of the Transfer of a Group Singing Intervention for Postnatal Depression from the United Kingdom to Denmark, Romania, and Italy
paper_abstract: Background: A ten-week group singing programme for mothers with symptoms of postnatal depression (PND) has been evaluated in two randomised controlled trials in the United Kingdom. Under the coordination of the World Health Organization (WHO) Regional Office for Europe, it was subsequently implemented in Denmark, Romania, and Italy. It is unclear which components of the programme transferred unchanged, which were adapted, and how strong the underlying evidence is. Methods: We conducted a structured comparative review of four primary studies: two British trials and two implementation studies. The intervention in each setting was described using the TIDieR checklist. Adaptations were coded using the FRAME framework, and outcomes were mapped to the RE-AIM dimensions. Risk of bias was appraised with RoB 2 (randomised trials) and the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (other designs). Certainty of evidence was judged using GRADE principles. Where possible, we calculated standardised effect sizes and absolute differences in retention. Results: In the larger trial (N = 199), mothers in the singing group had lower Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) scores than an active community control group at week 20 (treatment effect −1.59; approximately 0.41 baseline standard deviations) and week 36 (−1.56; approximately 0.40). The effect was not significant in an available-data analysis, and the trial was judged at high risk of bias because of differential attrition. Retention was 28 percentage points higher in the singing group at week 36 (66% vs. 38%). In Italy, 23 mothers attended a mean of 87% of sessions and none dropped out. Across settings, four components were retained everywhere: the ten-week group format, a trained singing leader, the presence of infants, and a non-medical framing. Recruitment, venue, session length, staffing, and repertoire were modified. Thirteen modifications were coded, of which nine were planned and three unplanned. Attitudes to mental illness and trust in health services shaped implementation more than language did. Conclusions: The programme's core transferred intact, and its acceptability was consistently high. Certainty that it reduces depressive symptoms is low, and there is no controlled evidence of effectiveness outside the United Kingdom.

paper_title: UAV Communication Security: A Narrative Review of Lightweight Authentication, ECC, and Hardware-Software Trade-Offs
paper_abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles increasingly exchange commands, telemetry, and mission data through interconnected ground, edge, and aerial networks. Their communication security depends on authentication, key management, implementation assurance, and constrained resources rather than on a cryptographic primitive alone. This narrative review examines lightweight authentication for UAV networks, with emphasis on the role of elliptic curve cryptography (ECC) and the trade-offs among software, FPGA, and hybrid implementations. Representative protocol studies are organized by communicating parties, trust assumptions, supporting mechanisms, and reported evidence. Standards for authenticated key establishment, authenticated encryption, and post-quantum cryptography provide a separate reference layer. The synthesis distinguishes mathematical security claims, symbolic protocol analysis, software timing, hardware realization, and operational deployment. ECC can support compact classical public-key mechanisms, but it does not independently provide message confidentiality, replay protection, capture resistance, or quantum resistance. PUF-assisted and infrastructure-assisted designs redistribute trust and implementation costs rather than eliminating them. A reporting framework identifies the information needed for meaningful comparisons, including credential provisioning, state recovery, communication overhead, and end-to-end energy. The review presents no new authentication protocol or experimental benchmark; its contribution is a critical, implementation-aware organization of the evidence and research gaps.

paper_title: Grid-Forming Electric Vehicles: A Critical Review of Bidirectional Charging, AI-Enabled Control, and Grid-Support Services
paper_abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) are evolving from passive charging loads into grid-supporting resources. Conventional smart-charging and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) strategies treat the charger as a grid-following current source that depends on a stiff external voltage, a dependence that becomes a weakness as inverter-based resources displace synchronous inertia. Grid-forming (GFM) control instead operates the bidirectional charger as a voltage source that establishes local voltage and frequency, enabling weak-grid, islanded, and black-start operation. This review synthesizes 113 sources, most identified through a structured keyword-based search, and organizes them along an evolutionary framework running from conventional charging through V2G and GFM EVs to AI-adaptive, fleet-coordinated resources. It covers bidirectional converter topologies; droop, virtual synchronous machine, virtual oscillator, and matching control; AI-enabled control using neural, fuzzy, reinforcement-learning, predictive, and physics-informed methods; fleet aggregation; resilience and black start; battery constraints; and cybersecurity and standardization. Throughout, experimentally demonstrated capability is distinguished from simulation-only or theoretical results. The synthesis shows that documented field pilots still rely on grid-following control and that GFM-EV validation remains largely confined to simulation. Seven research gaps are identified, including experimental validation, AI verifiability, battery–grid objective conflict, and fleet-scale coordination, and a five-generation roadmap toward autonomous, resilient GFM-EV fleets is proposed.

paper_title: Taxonomic Survey of Culture-Enriched Metagenomes from Gram-Negative Bacteria in Pigs, Piggery Environments, and Humans Associated with Pig Production Systems in Okada, Edo State, Nigeria
paper_abstract: Pig farming significantly supports livestock agriculture, food security, livelihoods, household income, and employment across developing countries, including Nigeria. This study characterized Gram-negative bacteria from pig production systems at Okada, Edo State, Nigeria, using a One Health approach of integrating animal, environmental and human-associated compartments. A total of 356 samples were collected and examined from the three compartments comprising, 132 pig-associated (37.08%), 124 environmental (34.83%), and 100 human-associated (28.09%). Cultural and biochemical examinations yielded 48 Gram-negative isolates, consisting of 22 isolates (45.83%) from pigs, 14 isolates (29.17%) from environmental sources, and 12 isolates (25.00%) from humans. The isolates comprised Proteus, Enterobacter, Pseudomonas, Escherichia, Klebsiella, Bordetella, Morganella, Providencia and Citrobacter, with Proteus predominating (13; 27.08%). Although bacterial genera varied numerically among compartments, Pearson’s chi-square test showed no significant association between bacterial genus and compartment (χ² = 11.25, p = 0.79). Whole-genome shotgun sequencing generated high-quality data, with mean reads exceeding 17 million and Q30 scores, with 95.50–96.50% of reads retained after filtering. Krona analysis showed predominance of Proteobacteria, Gammaproteobacteria and Enterobacterales across the compartments. Proteus spp (> 20%) and Bordetella trematum(16%), were prominent among pig-associated sequences; Proteus spp (>22%) and Escherichia coli(14%), predominated among human-associated sequences; environmental profiles were more heterogeneous, with E. coli, Citrobacter freundii, Klebsiella variicola each contributing approximately 9%. Seventeen species and a genus Halomonas were identified, with nine species shared across the three compartments. Cochran’s Q test showed no significant difference in species representation (Q = 1.14, p = 0.57). Jaccard similarity was highest between environmental and human-associated compartments (0.733), indicating substantial taxonomic connectivity. Overall, the findings support integrated One Health surveillance of Gram-negative bacteria in pig production.

paper_title: Polysaccharide-Based Edible Coating As a Sustainable Preservation Technique for Post -Harvest Shelf-Life Extension of Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum): A Review
paper_abstract: The persistence Postharvest losses of Tomato and other perishable fruits rise an urgenet need biodegradable and environmentally benign preservation methods. Polysaccharide-based edible coatings have shown great potential as alternatives to conventional synthetic methods for postharvest treatments due to their film-forming ability, biodegradability, biocompatibility, antimicrobial, and antioxidant carrier capabilities. This review examines the application of polysaccharide edible coatings as a sustainable preservation technique for tomatoes and other selected perishable fruits by considering their sources, functional and structural properties, in edible coating applications, focusing on their concentrations and preservation outcomes. Findings from published studies reveal that polysaccharide-based coatings reduce physiological weight loss, respiration rate, softening, ethylene production, colour change, and microbial damage, while enhancing nutritional constituents, hence extending the overall postharvest shelf life. Depending on the polymer concentration, molecular properties, fruit species, storage temperature, and coating formulation, it further demonstrated that, incorporating coatings with two or more polysaccharides, essential oils, plant extracts, and nanoparticles show improved preservative properties. The study suggests further studies on the development of low-cost, multifunctional, food-safe, polysaccharide-based coatings, especially those sourced from agricultural waste and other locally available resources. Such innovations could significantly contribute to sustainable postharvest control, food security, and environmentally benign food packaging systems.

paper_title: Malware Detection with Autonomous Agents: A Review of Functional Roles, Datasets, and Coordination Readiness
paper_abstract: Large language models are increasingly written into malware detection systems, yet the literature reports them under a single label that obscures what they actually do, and existing surveys either treat agents in the abstract or malware detection without them. This review closes that gap. It is the first to examine the implemented strand of agent-based malware detection as a coordinated system rather than a catalogue of techniques, and to ask how well positioned the field is to support multi-agent operation. We make three contributions. First, we introduce a functional classification that groups each system by which of four roles the model fills, namely perception, reasoning and decision-making, adaptive monitoring, and collaborative learning, treating the mature body of standalone detectors as the foundation rather than the object of review. Second, from a corpus of recent primary studies we derive a modality-based dataset taxonomy, a map linking datasets to the role the model plays, and a pipeline-stage and role-coverage matrix for the agent-based systems. Third, we assess which existing detectors are structurally ready for agentisation and why. The analysis yields three findings. What varies across the field is not which model is used but where in the detection chain it sits. Role coverage is bimodal, with perception and reasoning served almost everywhere while adaptive monitoring is realised by a single system in the corpus and collaborative learning by none. And uniformly high reported accuracy reflects curated, single-split evaluation rather than robustness. Reading these together, the discriminating property for agentisation is whether a system exposes anything between input and verdict, which makes integration and orchestration, not the invention of new detectors, the principal open problem.

paper_title: From Detection to Investigation: A Survey of Foundation Models and Agents for Financial Fraud and Financial Crime
paper_abstract: Foundation models are extending research on financial fraud and financial crime from isolated risk detection to document understanding, relational analysis, and investigative workflows. A gap nevertheless separates model outputs from candidate evidence and actionable conclusions. This survey examines advances in six families of foundation models: language, vision, speech, temporal, graph, and tabular models. It compares their roles and limitations along two dimensions: the risk-control lifecycle and the directness of the supporting evidence. Existing studies show that pretraining can support representation reuse and the processing of unstructured information, with direct validation in some financial tasks. Cross-modal identity binding, information availability over time, report faithfulness, and case-level benefits require separate evaluation. Evidence on investigative agents spans prototypes, controlled tasks, expert assessments, and industry disclosures, which establish different aspects of workflow feasibility, task performance, and user assessment. Establishing gains in investigative efficiency and reductions in financial losses requires case-level comparative evidence. We examine entity and temporal alignment, the organization of candidate evidence, constrained tool execution, and investigative benchmark design, together with the implications of adversarial threats, privacy, fairness, and model risk governance. Research priorities should shift from expanding system functionality toward factual traceability, sufficient evidence for decisions, and reviewable actions.

paper_title: From 3D Scene Understanding to Hazard Forecasting: A Critical Review of Remote Sensing–Driven Emergency Digital Twins
paper_abstract: Emergency forecasts benefit from scene detail when it constrains the relevant physical process and reaches decision-makers in time. This critical review examines flood inundation, wildfire spread and marine drift through 148 sources and 16 purpose-selected study families. Within this selected corpus, four families develop dedicated 3D conversion, chiefly for hydraulic-domain or fuel-material preparation; the coding rule excludes routine terrain input and existing ocean analyses. Forecast cases mainly update states, controls or initial trajectories. Hydraulic connectivity can alter local inundation. Corrected fire fronts remain exposed to propagation error, while wider marine search regions improve coverage at increased search cost. These mechanisms explain why geometric accuracy and analysis fit alone cannot establish predictive value. We propose a framework that selects scene attributes, update targets and observation timing jointly. Matched alternatives share a future response quantity, information cutoff and resource budget; deployment-specific tolerances connect their comparison to evacuation requirements and search capacity. Physically coupled neural representations require calibrated material properties and an online delivery-time account. The proposed tests assess the forecast effect of additional scene detail, the persistence of a correction and the time left for response.

paper_title: Impacts and Adaptations to Extreme Weather Events on Pathology Laboratories: A Scoping Review
paper_abstract: Pathology laboratories are a critical dependency across almost every diagnostic and treatment pathway. Pathology laboratories support healthcare delivery through analysing blood, urine, faecal and tissue samples, informing clinical diagnosis and tailoring patient treatment. However, laboratories have unique vulnerabilities to extreme weather events. To analyse samples and provide timely results, laboratories need highly-controlled environments and timelines. EWE can disrupt these and, when pathology laboratories fail or slow down during EWE, many healthcare services are disrupted simultaneously. In this study we have reviewed the impacts of heatwaves and flooding on pathology laboratories in G20 and European Union countries and any adaptation strategies that laboratories have put in place to mitigate those impacts. The PRISMA guidance was followed for a systematic search strategy that identified 1,133 articles for screening. Seven of these were included after full-text screening. Together with an additional two articles from backward citation searches, a total of nine articles were included in this review. Three reviewers were involved in this process. We found reports of widespread impacts of heatwaves and flooding on pathology laboratory staff, equipment, operations and internal and external supply chains. The perspectives of patients were mostly absent. While there were examples of adaptations deployed, we found little evidence of systematic evaluation to determine the cost-benefit of these adaptations, their health consequences or their impacts on health inequalities. Climate change will lead to more intense, frequent, volatile and unpredictable extreme weather events in most countries, which will increase pathology laboratory disruptions and subsequent impacts on healthcare pathways and patients. This should be a call for further action and the development of frameworks to enable pathology laboratories to implement and evaluate adaptations to extreme weather events-related disruptions that minimise disruption and deliver resilient pathology service provision to support patient care.

paper_title: Clinical Photography in UK Podiatric Practice A Narrative Review of Consent, Confidentiality and Safe Image Handling
paper_abstract: A clinical photograph can show changes that are difficult to describe in words. In podiatry, images help document wounds and skin lesions, support referrals and compare progress over time. They also create a lasting record that may identify the patient, even when the face is absent. This narrative review brings together UK legislation, professional guidance and selected literature to explain how photographs should be taken, stored and used. The starting point is the intended purpose. Agreement to a photograph for care does not automatically permit teaching, research, publication or promotion, and the patient’s agreement is distinct from the organisation’s data-protection basis for processing the image. The proposed framework covers the patient discussion, image capture, record linkage, storage, secondary use and audit. Its practical message is simple: a clinical photograph needs the same care as the rest of the patient’s health record.

paper_title: MCDM Applications for Sustainability Assessment in Textile and Apparel Supply Chains: A Systematic Review of Methods, Contexts, and Criteria
paper_abstract: Sustainability in the textile supply chain involves complex trade-offs across economic, environmental and social aspects, driven by the variability in materials, manufacturing processes and technologies, industrial management, geographical locations, working conditions, logistics, and product use. While multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) methods have been increasingly applied to navigate these trade-offs, existing reviews have narrowly focused on bibliometric trends, offering limited insight into the contextual application and sustainability criteria used in these assessments. This study addresses this gap through a systematic literature review by analysing 96 studies that investigate the application of MCDM methods in sustainability management across the textile supply chain, with specific attention to methodological rigor and contextual relevance. The review identifies two key research dimensions: (1) the MCDM methods employed and their application contexts in respective scope of studies, and (2) the applied and prioritized criteria for sustainability management in textile industries. Results show that the identification of influential factors for sustainability implementation is the most common scope of study, with DEMATEL being the dominant MCDM tool and identifying government policies as the most influential factor. This is followed by sustainable supplier selection, with frequent use of hybrid AHP-TOPSIS methods, often in fuzzy settings, and a predominant focus on economic criteria, particularly cost and financial flexibility. The majority of corporate sustainability assessments rely on quantitative environmental data derived from corporate reports, and public data and use single-method MCDM models without explicit weighting schemes. Product-level assessments commonly employ distance-based MCDM methods to support the interpretation of Life Cycle Assessment results or to expand the sustainability perspective by incorporating economic and social dimensions. This review advances the understanding of how MCDM methods support sustainability decision-making in different contexts and settings of textile supply chain and highlights key criteria shaping such evaluations.

paper_title: Continuous Risk-Based Scheduling for Food Safety Inspection: Integrating Historical Decay with Event-Driven Consumer Review Signals
paper_abstract: Batch risk-based inspection scheduling struggles to detect a critical failure class: food facilities with recent clean inspections that subsequently develop severe violations. Traditional systems recompute risk on fixed planning cycles using static historical data, leaving blind spots between inspection cycles. To address this, we introduce the Continuous Inspection Risk (CIR) system, an event-driven scheduling pipeline that re-ranks the inspection queue dynamically as new data arrives. CIR combines a decay-weighted historical score with a stream of real-time consumer reviews triaged by a language-model classifier. A key structural contribution is our temporal partition rule, which strictly excludes reviews predating the most recent inspection to prevent superseded signals from skewing current risk. Evaluating CIR on 9,505 routine inspections in Santa Clara County, California (2024-2026), we show that history-based scoring alone reduces mean time-to-detection of major violations by 69 days (20.9%) under a 30% inspection budget, but fails to anticipate severe vermin-related closures (0/8 detected). Incorporating post-inspection review signals drastically improves performance, predicting 7 of 8 vermin closures with an average lead time of 117 days-firing on the exact day of review publication in four instances. Introducing a review corroboration rule improves precision from 0.70 to 0.78 without loss of recall. Finally, we analyze critical implementation challenges, documenting a data-hygiene pitfall (stale review leakage across inspection boundaries) and an evaluation limitation involving unobserved facility self-remediation. This work provides the first case-level evaluation of event-driven inspection triggering using open data and provides a reproducible benchmark for review-augmented public health systems

paper_title: Probable but Not Valid: A Psychometric Audit of Decision Models as Synthetic Survey Respondents
paper_abstract: Language models are increasingly used to create synthetic survey samples, also called silicon samples. Decision models are a new class of language models that return a probability for each point of a rating scale instead of text. We ask whether these models, or the newest generative LLMs, can stand in for human respondents on a psychometric survey. We test fourteen decision models from eleven providers and 47 generative LLMs on an open Lithuanian organisational-psychology survey (n=263, 68 items), with 100 real respondent profiles, the Psychometric Similarity Score (PSS) and statistical baselines. The best generative model, MiniMax M3, reaches PSS 0.813. This is level with a Gaussian copula fit only on other respondents (0.824) and below a copula fit in sample (0.927). A second sample of 100 real people scores below the best models, so at this size PSS cannot rank them against real respondents. In 5 of 10 product lines the newest generative release scores below an earlier release of the same line beyond resampling noise, and none gains beyond it. With the default rounded readout, 13 of 14 decision models score below the generative reference gpt-5.4-mini. Of the 47 generative models, 33 reproduce the pattern of item correlations better than any decision model. Averaged over respondents, the probability vectors are much closer to the human item marginals than rounded answers. They also rank respondents about as well as a profile regression fit on 163 real people. As forecasts of each person's own answers, however, every decision model is worse than the answer frequencies of other respondents, mainly because its average vector differs from them. The profile regression improves on these frequencies by only 1.0%, so the profile fields say little about how a person answers. Synthetic respondents built on such profiles should therefore aim at sample-level fidelity.
comments: 36 pages, 6 figures, 16 tables. Code, raw model outputs and tables are available from the corresponding author on request

paper_title: Signal-Amplification Strategies for Gold-Nanoparticle Lateral Flow Assays: A Structured Review of Limit-of-Detection Improvement Relative to Conventional GNP-LFA
paper_abstract: Gold-nanoparticle lateral flow assays (GNP-LFAs) are attractive for point-of-care testing, but their conventional colorimetric readout often limits analytical sensitivity. This structured review asked which signal-amplification strategies produce the greatest improvement in limit of detection (LOD) relative to a conventional GNP-LFA comparator, and by what magnitude. Candidate records were identified through an investigator-directed keyword search and screened at full text by a single reviewer; 29 of 36 assessed records met eligibility, contributing 36 comparator arms across nine mechanism categories. Reported LOD fold-improvements ranged from no measurable gain to 1000x. Enzyme/catalytic (nanozyme) amplification spanned the widest range (4x–1000x across 5 arms), whereas silver/gold enhancement was the most frequently reported category (7 arms, 4 studies), with gains mostly below 40x and one study reporting up to 488x. Two arms showed no meaningful improvement over a conventional or visual-readout comparator. Gains varied substantially within and between categories and were analyte- and format-dependent; same-study and literature-baseline comparators answer different questions and should not be treated interchangeably. The largest gains came from mechanisms acting on detection chemistry rather than flow control or label loading, although most categories rest on few independent studies. Single-reviewer screening and an investigator-directed search are limitations.

paper_title: Integrated Development of Spatial Regeneration and the Cultural and Creative Industries in Chinese Traditional Villages: A Correlational Literature Review
paper_abstract: Spatial regeneration and the cultural and creative industries (CCIs) are paired in policies for China’s traditional villages, yet seldom examined together. This correlational literature review analyzes the full texts of 35 peer-reviewed case studies published in 2017–2026. The corpus was assembled purposively; a later check of two bibliographic databases flagged at least 238 further potentially eligible records, so the 35 papers cover only part of the literature. Each paper was coded for regeneration strategies, CCI categories, village type, governance mode, outcomes, and conflicts, and the analysis combines keyword co-occurrence, φ coefficients, and a qualitative classification of outcomes. Five of six regeneration strategies are reported in more than two-thirds of the papers. Cultural tourism is reported in every paper, followed by performing arts, crafts, and museums, whereas architecture, design, film, and digital content appear in eight papers. No strategy–category association remains significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Of 140 outcome judgments, 47.1% are realized positive, 35.7% mixed, and 10.0% realized negative; negative results concentrate in the social dimension. The sample is too small to test differences by region, village type, or governance mode. In these papers, the link between spatial regeneration and cultural activity is documented almost exclusively through tourism.

paper_title: From Prediction to Decision: A Critical Review of AI Agents for Cancer Treatment and the Evaluation Gap
paper_abstract: Artificial intelligence for cancer treatment is undergoing a transition from predicting outcomes to supporting decisions.
